(p-٧٨٤) فَإنْ قِيلَ: فَقَدْ قالَ النَّبِيُّ (ﷺ) لِابْنِ عَبّاسٍ: «اللَّهُمَّ فَقِّهْهُ في الدِّينِ وعَلِّمْهُ التَّأْوِيلَ». قِيلَ: أمّا تَأْوِيلُ الأمْرِ والنَّهْيِ فَذاكَ يَعْلَمُهُ، واللّامُ هُنا لِلتَّأْوِيلِ المَعْهُودِ، لَمْ يَقُلْ: تَأْوِيلَ كُلِّ القُرْآنِ. فالتَّأْوِيلُ المَنفِيُّ هو تَأْوِيلُ الأخْبارِ الَّتِي لا يَعْلَمُ حَقِيقَةَ مَخْبَرِها إلّا اللَّهُ، والتَّأْوِيلُ المَعْلُومُ هو الأمْرُ الَّذِي يَعْلَمُ العِبادُ تَأْوِيلَهُ. وهَذا كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إلا تَأْوِيلَهُ يَوْمَ يَأْتِي تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾ وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِما لَمْ يُحِيطُوا بِعِلْمِهِ ولَمّا يَأْتِهِمْ تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾ فَإنَّ المُرادَ تَأْوِيلُ الخَبَرِ الَّذِي فِيهِ عَنْ المُسْتَقْبَلِ، فَإنَّهُ هو الَّذِي يُنْتَظَرُ ويَأْتِي، ولَمّا يَأْتِهِمْ. وأمّا تَأْوِيلُ الأمْرِ والنَّهْيِ فَذاكَ في الأمْرِ، وتَأْوِيلُ الخَبَرِ عَنْ اللَّهِ وعَمَّنْ مَضى إنْ أُدْخِلَ في التَّأْوِيلِ لا يُنْتَظَرُ، واللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ أعْلَمُ وبِهِ التَّوْفِيقُ. انْتَهى كَلامُ الشَّيْخِ تَقِيِّ الدِّينِ (Taqi al-Din, i.e. Ibn Taymiyya). وإنَّما سُقْتُهُ بِطُولِهِ لِما أنَّ هَذا البَحْثَ مِنَ المَعارِكِ المُهِمَّةِ الَّتِي قَلَّ مَن حَرَّرَها ونَهَجَ فِيها مَنهَجَ الحَقِّ كالشَّيْخِ - قُدِّسَ سِرُّهُ -. ومَعَ ما في خِلالِ البَحْثِ مِنَ القَواعِدِ الجَلِيلَةِ في فَنِّ التَّفْسِيرِ. فَخُذْ ما أُوتِيتَ وكُنْ مِنَ الشّاكِرِينَ. واللَّهُ يَقُولُ الحَقَّ وهو يَهْدِي السَّبِيلَ.

(p-٧٨٥) وقالَ الإمامُ الجَلِيلُ أبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ المُرْتَضى اليَمانِيُّ في كِتابِ (إيثارِ الحَقِّ عَلى الخَلْقِ) في بَحْثِ سَبَبِ الِاخْتِلافِ الشَّدِيدِ بَيْنَ الفِرَقِ ما نَصُّهُ:
وأمّا الأصْلُ الثّانِي وهو السَّمْعُ فَهو اخْتِلافُهم في أمْرَيْنِ:
أحَدُهُما: في مَعْرِفَةِ المُحْكَمِ والمُتَشابِهِ أنْفُسِهِما والتَّمْيِيزِ بَيْنَهُما حَتّى يُرَدَّ المُتَشابِهُ إلى المُحْكَمِ.
وثانِيهِما: اخْتِلافُهم هَلْ يَعْلَمُونَ تَأْوِيلَ المُتَشابِهِ، ثُمَّ اخْتِلافُهم في تَأْوِيلِهِ عَلى تَسْلِيمِ أنَّهم قَدْ عَرَفُوا المُتَشابِهَ.
[The author's words have been abridged due to their great length.]

(p-797)The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[8] ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.﴾

﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾ is from the speech of those firmly grounded in knowledge (al-Rasikhun), meaning: do not incline our hearts away from guidance after You have set them upon it, and do not make them like those in whose hearts is deviation (zaygh), who follow what is ambiguous (mutashabih) of the Qur'an. Rather, keep us firm upon Your straight path. ﴿And grant us from Yourself mercy﴾ by which our hearts may be made firm. ﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾, abundant in blessings and bounty, lavish in gifts and grants. In this is evidence that guidance and misguidance are from Him, exalted is He. And from ʿĀ'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, she said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would often supplicate: 'O Turner of the hearts, keep my heart firm upon Your religion.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! How often you supplicate with this supplication!' He said: 'There is no heart but that it is between two of the fingers of the All-Merciful. If He wills to make it upright, He makes it upright, and if He wills to make it deviate, He makes it deviate.'" It is in the Sahih and the Sunan.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[9] ﴿Our Lord, You are the Gatherer of mankind for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.﴾

﴿Our Lord, You are the Gatherer of mankind for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.﴾ This is part of the speech of those firmly grounded in knowledge (al-Rasikhun fi al-'ilm). That is because, when they asked Allah Exalted to preserve them from deviation (al-zaygh) and to single them out with guidance and mercy, it is as if they were saying: the purpose of this request is not what concerns the benefits of this world, for it is finite and passing away. Rather, the greater purpose of it is what concerns the Hereafter, for it is the true goal and the final destination. We know, O our God, that You are the Gatherer of mankind for recompense on the Day of Resurrection, and we know that Your promise will not be broken. Whoever's heart has deviated will remain there in punishment forever, and whomever You have granted mercy and guidance will remain there in happiness and honour forever. So the greatest purpose of this supplication is what concerns the Hereafter. This was stated by al-Razi. Then he said: al-Jubba'i argued with this verse for the certainty of the threat against sinners (al-fussaq). He said: that is because the threat falls under the wording of promise, by the evidence of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised to be true; have you found what your Lord promised to be true?﴾ [al-A'raf: 44]. And promise (al-wa'd), appointment (al-mau'id) and tryst (al-mi'ad) are one and the same. He has informed in this verse that He does not fail the appointment. So this was evidence that He does not fail in threat. The answer: we do not concede that He threatens sinners absolutely; rather that threat, according to us, is conditional upon the condition of non-pardon, just as it is by consensus conditional upon the condition of non-repentance. Just as you established that condition by a separate evidence, so we established the condition of non-pardon by a separate evidence. Even if we concede that He threatens them, we do not concede that the threat falls under the wording of promise. As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?﴾ [al-A'raf: 44], we say: why could that not be like His saying: ﴿So give them good tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 24] (p-799) and His saying: ﴿Taste, indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [al-Dukhan: 49]? Also, why could it not be that what is meant is that they used to expect from their idols that they would intercede for them with Allah, so the promise meant those benefits?

Al-Wahidi mentioned in (al-Basit) another approach, saying: why could this not be taken to refer to the appointment of the friends (of Allah), rather than the threat against the enemies? Because breaking a threat is considered generosity among the Arabs. He said: the evidence for this is that they praise one another for it. The poet said:

When he promises good fortune, he fulfils his promise, and if he threatens hardship, pardon prevents it.

And he related the debate that took place between Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' and 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said to 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd: What do you say about the people of major sins? He said: I say that Allah made a promise and issued a threat; so He fulfils His threat just as He fulfils His promise. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: You are a foreigner (a'jam), not in the tongue, I mean, but a foreigner in heart. The Arabs regard going back on a promise as baseness (luʾm), and going back on a threat as generosity (karam). And he recited:

And indeed I, if I threaten him or promise him, am one who lies about my threat, and one who fulfils my promise.

Know that the Mu'tazilah reported that when Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said this statement, 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd said to him: O Abu 'Amr, is God called "one who denies His own self"? He said: No. 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd said: Then your argument has fallen. They said: Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' was silenced.

In my view, Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' could have answered this question by saying: you have analogised the threat to the promise, whereas I only mentioned this to show the difference between the two categories. That is because the promise is a right owed by Him, and the threat is a right belonging to Him; whoever waives his own right has shown generosity and nobility, whereas whoever waives the right of another (p-800) has shown baseness. The difference between promise and threat thus becomes clear, and your analogy is refuted. I mentioned this verse only to clarify this difference. As for your saying: if He did not act, He would become a liar and one who denies His own self, its answer is: this would only follow if the threat were established definitively without any condition. In my view, all threats are conditional upon non-pardon, so abandoning it does not entail the entry of falsehood into the speech of Allah Exalted. This is what relates to this account. And Allah knows best.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[10] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—their wealth will not avail them, nor their children, against Allah at all. And they are the fuel of the Fire.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—their wealth will not avail them﴾: that which they expend in acquiring benefits and warding off harms. ﴿Nor their children﴾: those by whom they support one another in important matters. ﴿Against Allah﴾: that is, against His punishment, may He be exalted. ﴿At all﴾: of averting. That is, they will not repel any of His punishment from themselves. It is said: "So-and-so did not avail anything," meaning he did not benefit in an important matter and did not suffice for a need. And "a man who is mughnin" means one who is sufficient and adequate, as said by al-Azhari. A parallel to this verse is His Exalted saying: ﴿The day when neither wealth nor children will benefit﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 88] ﴿except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 89]. ﴿And they are the fuel of the Fire﴾: with the vowel fatha on the waw (waqud), meaning its firewood. It has also been read with a damma (wuqud), meaning the people of its fuel. Most of the lexicographers hold that the damma is the verbal noun, meaning "the kindling," while the fatha denotes the firewood. Al-Zajjaj said: the verbal noun is with damma, and fatha is permissible in it. This is like His Exalted saying: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be arriving thereto﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98].

(p-801)

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 11:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[11] ﴿As was the case with the people of Pharaoh and those before them, who denied Our signs. So Allah seized them for their sins, and Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

﴿As was the case with the people of Pharaoh﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: the way of these people in disbelief is like the way of the people of Pharaoh. Al-da'b (with a sukun, and it may also be vocalized with a fatha) is a verbal noun of da'aba in an action, when one exerts oneself in it. It is used figuratively for what a person is characterized by in his affairs and condition. It is said: "This is your da'b," i.e., your affair and your practice. Al-Azhari said, quoting al-Zajjaj regarding this verse: i.e., like the matter of the people of Pharaoh. This is what the lexicographers said. Al-Azhari said: "The view I hold regarding it, and Allah knows best, is that their da'b here is their striving in their disbelief and their collaboration against the Prophet ﷺ, like the collaboration of the people of Pharaoh against Moses, peace be upon him. It is said: da'abtu, adha'u, da'aban and da'uban, when I strove at a thing." End of quotation. Abu al-Baqa' said: In this there is a warning to them, given their knowledge of what befell the people of Pharaoh.

﴿And those before them﴾, i.e., before the people of Pharaoh, from the disbelieving nations. The relative pronoun is in the genitive position, coordinated with what precedes it.

﴿denied Our signs﴾ is an explanation and clarification of their da'b, which they practiced, in the manner of a resumptive statement built upon an implied question.

﴿So Allah seized them for their sins﴾, i.e., He punished and destroyed them because of them.

﴿And Allah is severe in punishment﴾, i.e., the seizing for sin. In it is a magnification of the act of seizing and an increase in warning to the disbelievers.

The commentary on His saying, the Exalted:

[12] ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and it is an evil resting-place.﴾

﴿Say to those who disbelieve﴾ in this religion, and they are the Jews (according to the narration that follows), or the Christians of Najran, because the surah was revealed to establish the truth with them. Or it is more general. ﴿You will be overcome﴾, that is, in this world. ﴿And gathered﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿to Hell, and it is an evil resting-place﴾, the bed. That is, your disbelief is like the disbelief of the people of Pharaoh toward Musa. Quraysh were dealt with for their disbelief in the way you have seen, so you will be dealt with as they were, and [p. 802] that is, you will be overcome as they were overcome. God has fulfilled His promise by the killing of Qurayza, the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir, the conquest of Khaybar, and the imposition of the jizya (poll tax) on others than them. This is one of the clearest proofs of prophethood.

Abu Dawud related in his Sunan, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, through the route of Ibn Ishaq, from Ibn Abbas: "When the Messenger of God ﷺ had inflicted on the people of Badr what he inflicted, and returned to Madinah, he gathered the Jews in the market of Banu Qaynuqa' and said: 'O assembly of Jews! Embrace Islam before God inflicts on you what He inflicted on Quraysh.' They said: 'O Muhammad! Do not let yourself be deceived by the fact that you killed a few men of Quraysh, who were inexperienced and did not know how to fight. By God, if you fought us you would know that we are the people, and that you have not met the likes of us.' So God revealed: ﴿Say to those who﴾ to His saying: ﴿for those endowed with insight﴾ [Al 'Imran: 13]."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[13] ﴿There has already been a sign for you in the two armies that met: one fighting in the way of Allah, and another disbelieving, who saw them as twice their number by sight. And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed, in that is a lesson for those who have vision.﴾

﴿There has already been for you﴾ O disbelievers, whose mention has preceded: ﴿a sign﴾, a lesson and an indication that you will be overcome, and that Allah strengthens His religion, supports His Messenger, and exalts His command. ﴿In two armies﴾, i.e., two groups, ﴿that met﴾ on the day of Badr for battle. ﴿One fighting in the way of Allah﴾, i.e., in His obedience, and they were the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions, (p-803) and they were three hundred and thirteen men, with them were horsemen, two horses, and eight swords, and most of them were foot soldiers. ﴿And another disbelieving﴾, and they were the polytheists of Quraysh, who were nearly a thousand. ﴿Who saw them as twice their number﴾, i.e., the polytheists saw the Muslims as twice the number of the polytheists, nearly two thousand. Allah showed them, despite their small number, as multiples of them, so that the polytheists would be awed by them and would shrink from fighting them. This was a reinforcement for them from Allah, exalted is He, just as He reinforced them with the angels.

If you say: This contradicts His saying in Surah al-Anfal: ﴿And He makes you appear few in their eyes﴾ [al-Anfal: 44]. I say: They were first made to appear few in their eyes, until they became bold against them. When they met them, they appeared many in their eyes, until they were defeated. So the making few and the making many occurred in two different states. A parallel to this, in what is understood as differing circumstances, is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So on that Day no one will be questioned about his sin, neither man nor jinn﴾ [al-Rahman: 39], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ [al-Saffat: 24]. Making them appear few at one time and many at another in their eyes is more emphatic in power and in showing the sign. Thus [it is stated] in (al-Kashshaf). I say: It may also be answered that they were first made to appear many in their eyes so that terror, fear, dismay, and panic would take hold of them. Then, when the lines were formed and the two groups met, Allah made these appear few in the eyes of those, so that each of them would advance upon the other, that Allah might accomplish a matter that was already decreed.

﴿By sight﴾, meaning: a clear and manifest seeing without any ambiguity in it, a direct witnessing like all other direct witnessings. Thus [it is stated] in (al-Kashshaf).

﴿And Allah supports﴾, i.e., strengthens, ﴿with His victory whom He wills. Indeed, in that﴾, i.e., in the multiplying and the making few, and the overcoming of the few over the many, despite lacking equipment, against the many who were armed with weapons, ﴿is a lesson﴾, i.e., a reason for consideration, a sign, and an admonition, ﴿for those who have vision﴾, for those possessing intellects and insight.

(p-804)

The Explanation of His Words, the Exalted:

[14] ﴿Made attractive to people is the love of desires: women and sons, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, livestock, and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, but with Allah is the best return.﴾

﴿Made attractive to people﴾ is a resumed statement, brought to explain the lowliness of the worldly portions in all their kinds, to make people renounce them, and to direct their desires toward what is with Him, the Exalted, after explaining that they do not benefit the disbelievers who used to take pride in them. By "people" is meant the category (jins), as Abu al-Su'ud said. ﴿The love of desires﴾, i.e., the desirable things; it is expressed this way as an exaggeration of their being desired and sought after, or as a debasement of them, because desire is considered contemptible by the wise, and whoever follows it is blameworthy, bearing witness against himself to his animality. ﴿Of women﴾: placing them first indicates their preeminence in the meaning of desire, since the most complete of pleasures is obtained from them. ﴿And sons﴾: for multiplying through them, hoping they will take the place of their fathers after them, and for boasting and adornment. ﴿And heaped-up piles﴾: i.e., abundant wealth. His saying ﴿al-muqantarah (heaped-up)﴾ is derived from it for emphasis, like their saying "alf mu'allafah (a thousand gathered)," "badrah mubaddarah (a purse scattered)," "ibil mu'abbalah (camels herded)," and "darahim mudarhamah (dirhams hoarded)." ﴿Of gold and silver﴾: al-Razi said: They are beloved only because they have been made the price of all things, so whoever owns them is as one who owns all things, and the quality of ownership is power, and power is an attribute of perfection, and perfection is loved for its own sake. Since gold and silver are the most perfect means of attaining this perfection, which is loved for its own sake, and what the beloved cannot be obtained without is itself beloved, they are indeed beloved. ﴿And branded horses﴾: i.e., those sent out to pasture, roaming wherever they wish, or those bearing the sima, i.e., the mark. Abu Muslim said: What is meant by these marks is the white blazes and markings found on horses, namely that the mares are marked with white on the face and legs. ﴿And livestock﴾: plural of na'am, which are camels, cattle, and sheep, for acquiring growing wealth. ﴿And tilled land﴾: i.e., land prepared for planting and cultivation. ﴿That﴾: i.e., what has been mentioned. ﴿Is the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾: one enjoys it therein, then it perishes. ﴿But with Allah is the best return﴾: i.e., the place of return, which is Paradise; so desire should be directed toward it and not toward anything else. In its implication is a condemnation of those who magnify those desires and covet them greatly, and who prefer seeking them over seeking what is with Allah, as well as an encouragement to renounce the world and a desire for the Hereafter.

Note:

In the making attractive of these mentioned matters to people is an indication of the trial they contain:

As for women, it is in the Sahih that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have left after me no trial more harmful to men than women."

As for sons, in the Musnad of Abu Ya'la from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "A child is a fruit of the heart, and it is a cause of cowardice, a cause of miserliness, and a cause of sorrow." That is: a father becomes cowardly in jihad out of fear for his offspring, refrains from spending in obedience out of fear of poverty, and grieves over their illness out of fear of their death. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾ [al-Taghabun: 14]. It was said to one of the ascetics: "Why do you not seek what Allah has written for you?" He said: "I hear and obey the command of Allah, but no welcome to one who, if he lives, tempts me, and if he dies, saddens me." He means His saying: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and with Allah is a great reward﴾ [al-Taghabun: 15].

As for heaped-up piles: the verse before it is about them, and His saying: ﴿Nay, indeed, man transgresses﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6] ﴿when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq: 7], and He said: ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself﴾ [al-Isra': 83]. Nothing produces insolence like wealth, and through it are gathered the causes of nobility, leadership, glory, and boasting.

As for horses: they may become a burden upon their owner when he ties them for boasting, showing off, and as a provocation to the people of Islam, as in the Sahih, and in the Musnad of Ahmad from Ibn Mas'ud, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Horses are of three kinds: a horse for the Merciful, a horse for the human being, and a horse for the Devil. As for the horse for the Merciful, it is the one tied in the way of Allah; its fodder, dung, and urine [are in its scales on the Day of Judgment], and he mentioned what Allah willed. As for the horse of the Devil, it is the one wagered upon or gambled over. As for the horse of the human being, it is the horse a person keeps seeking to increase its progeny, and it is a covering from poverty."

As for the trial of livestock and tilled land, it is in the same meaning as what has preceded. And Allah knows best.

When the Exalted mentioned what is with Him of the best return in summary, He pointed to its details, to exaggerate in encouraging it, and said:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[15] ﴿Say, "Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who fear Allah are gardens with their Lord, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and purified spouses, and approval from Allah." And Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.﴾

﴿Say, "Shall I inform you of something better than that?"﴾ That is, than the desires made attractive to you. ﴿For those who fear Allah﴾ and did not immerse themselves in their desires: ﴿with their Lord are gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ of various kinds of drinks: of honey, milk, wine, and water, and other things that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that have not occurred to the heart of any human being. The phrase ﴿for those who fear Allah﴾ is the predicate of the subject ﴿gardens﴾, and ﴿flow﴾ is its attribute. The word ﴿with﴾ ('inda) is either connected to what the preposition governs in terms of the meaning of settledness, or it is originally an attribute of the gardens which was fronted and therefore became accusative as a circumstantial complement (ḥāl). The sense of "with" indicates the complete loftiness of the rank of the gardens and the exalted nature of their level. ﴿Abiding therein﴾ means remaining therein forever and ever, not seeking any change from them. ﴿And purified spouses﴾ means purified from bodily and natural impurities and defects that generally do not free the women of this world. ﴿And approval from Allah﴾ — the tanwin here is for magnification, meaning an approval whose measure cannot be estimated. This spiritual pleasure completes the bodily pleasures they have attained and is the greatest of them, as the Exalted said in the verse of Bara'a: ﴿And approval from Allah is greater﴾ [al-Tawba: 72], meaning: the greatest of the eternal blessings He has given them. Al-Shaykhan narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to the people of Paradise: 'O people of Paradise!' They say: 'Here we are, our Lord, at Your service and good pleasure.' He says: 'Are you pleased?' They say: 'And why would we not be pleased, when You have given us what You have not given any of Your creation?' He says: 'Shall I not give you something better than that?' They say: 'Our Lord, and what is better than that?' He says: 'I cause My approval to descend upon you, so I will never be displeased with you after it, forever.'" ﴿And Allah is Seeing of [His] servants﴾ means: He is Knowing of their interests, so they ought to be pleased with what He has chosen for them of the blessings of the Hereafter, and to renounce what He has made them renounce of worldly affairs. Then He, glorified be He, described those who feared Him, who thus succeeded and attained those honours, by His saying:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[16] ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."﴾

﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."﴾ Al-Hakim said: The verse indicates that it is permissible for one who supplicates to mention his acts of obedience and what he has drawn near to Allah with, and then to supplicate. It is supported by what is in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, the two authentic collections of Bukhari and Muslim) concerning the narration of the people of the cave, and each of them invoking Allah through the best of his deeds, then the Exalted Creator relieving them of their distress; and by His saying, exalted is He:

On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[17] ﴿The patient, the truthful, the obedient, those who spend, and those who ask forgiveness at dawn.﴾

﴿The patient﴾: that is, patient in hardship and adversity and at the time of battle. ﴿The truthful﴾: truthful in their faith, their words, and their intentions. ﴿The obedient﴾: those who are devoted to Allah, submissive to Him. ﴿Those who spend﴾: who spend their wealth in the way of Allah, Exalted is He, on kin, relatives, filling the needs of friends, and aiding those in need. ﴿Those who ask forgiveness at dawn﴾: ﴿al-asḥār﴾ is the plural of saḥar (with a fatha on both letters, or a fatha then a sukun), which is the time just before the break of dawn at the end of the night. One says "tasahhara" when he eats at that time. Al-Ḥarālī said: its implication is their night prayer, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 17–18].

Al-Rāzī said: know that what is meant by it is one who prays at night and then follows it with seeking forgiveness and supplication, because a person does not occupy himself with supplication and seeking forgiveness unless he has prayed before that. So His words, ﴿and those who ask forgiveness at dawn﴾, indicate that they had prayed during the night. — End.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar used to pray during the night, then he would say: "O Nafiʿ! Has the saḥar come?" When he said "Yes," he would devote himself to supplication and seeking forgiveness until morning. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas ibn Malik who said: "We were commanded, when we had prayed during the night, to seek forgiveness at the end of the saḥar seventy times." Ibn Jarir narrated from Ḥāṭib who said: "I heard a man at the saḥar in a corner of the mosque, saying: 'O Lord, You commanded me and I obeyed You, and this is the saḥar, so forgive me.' I looked, and it was Ibn Masʿud."

It is established in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs and other collections of hadith and sunan, through more than one chain, from a group of the Companions, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains. He says: 'Who will call upon Me that I may answer him? Who will ask of Me that I may give him? Who will seek My forgiveness that I may forgive him?'" And in a narration of Muslim: "Then He, Blessed and Exalted, extends His hands and says: 'Who will lend to One who is neither needy nor unjust?'" And in another narration: "until the dawn breaks."

The Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Kathir said: The Ḥāfiẓ Abu al-Ḥasan al-Dāraqutnī devoted a separate juz' to this subject, narrating it through multiple chains. It is related that some of the righteous said to his son: "My son! Let the rooster not be better than you: it calls at the saḥar while you are asleep." The wisdom in specifying the saḥar is that it is a time when people are heedless of exposing themselves to the divine breezes and the subtle mercies of the All-Holy; at that time worship is more arduous, intention is purer, desire is more abundant, along with His nearness, Exalted and Sanctified is He, to His servants. Al-Suyuti said: in the verse is the virtue of seeking forgiveness at the saḥar, and that this time is the best of times. Al-Rāzī said: know that seeking forgiveness at the saḥar has a special effect in strengthening faith and in the perfection of servitude.

The first: at the time of saḥar the light of dawn rises after darkness had enveloped everything, and by the rising of the light of dawn the dead become living; so there is a time of general generosity and complete outpouring. It is not far-fetched that, at the rising of the dawn of the great world, the dawn of the small world rises, which is the manifestation of the light of Allah's majesty in the heart.

The second: the time of saḥar is the most pleasant time for sleepers; so when the servant turns away from that pleasure and devotes himself to worship, obedience is more perfect.

The third: it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿and those who ask forgiveness at dawn﴾ means those who pray the Dawn prayer. — End.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this third view from Zayd ibn Aslam, and upon it, the prayer is called seeking forgiveness because they sought forgiveness through performing it.

A subtle point:

Al-Zamakhsharī said: the waw placed between the attributes serves to indicate their perfection in each one of them.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[18] ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He﴾ — that is, He knows, informs, or declares that there is no true deity other than His exalted Essence. The angels and those of knowledge bear witness to this by affirmation (al-iqrar). This is a noble rank for the scholars, since they are mentioned in the same breath as the honored angels in affirming Divine unity, by being joined to the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the phrase: ﴿standing in justice﴾, that is, with justice in His judgments. ﴿There is no god but He﴾ is repeated for emphasis, and so that upon it He builds His saying: ﴿the Mighty﴾, so that none can approach His sublime majesty; ﴿the Wise﴾, so that nothing proceeds from Him except in accordance with rectitude. Thus in (Jami' al-Bayan).

And in (al-Intisaf) it says: This repetition is for what I have already presented concerning its counterpart, in matters where the speech is introduced with tawhid and the time has grown long. The speech opens with tawhid, then follows the tawhid with the enumeration of those who bear witness to it, then His saying: ﴿standing in justice﴾, which is tanzih (transcendence). So the discourse lengthened with this, and so tawhid is renewed right after tanzih, to be followed by His saying: ﴿Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam﴾ [Al 'Imran: 19]. Had this renewal not occurred, the earlier tawhid would have been cut off in understanding from what was intended to be conveyed by it. And Allah knows best.

A subtle point:

al-Razi said: If it is said: the one who claims the oneness is Allah, so how can the one claiming be a witness?

The answer comes in several aspects:

The first: the true Witness is none other than Allah, because He is the One who created things and made them signs of His unity. Were it not for those signs, testimony would not be valid. Then, after establishing those signs, it is He who granted the scholars success in knowing them; were it not for the signs Allah established and guided them to, they would have been unable to reach through them the knowledge of unity. Then, after the knowledge of unity was attained, He granted them success until they guided others to the knowledge of tawhid. Since this is the case, the witness to unity is none but Allah alone, and for this reason He said: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say: "Allah"﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. Then he presented the remaining aspects, so consult it.

And the gnostic al-Sha'rani, may his secret be sanctified, said in the book (al-Jawahir wa'l-Durar): I asked my brother Afdal al-Din: Why did the Real, exalted is He, bear witness for Himself that there is no god but He? He said, may Allah be pleased with him: To alert His servants to His independence from their affirmation of His unity, and that He is the one who affirms His own oneness by Himself. I said to him: Why then did He join the angels to Himself rather than others? He said: Because their knowledge of tawhid was not acquired from reflection upon proofs as with humans; rather their knowledge of it was acquired from the Divine manifestation (al-tajalli al-ilahi), and that is the strongest and truest of knowledge. Therefore they were placed first in mention before the people of knowledge. Also, the angels are an intermediary between the Real and His messengers, so it was appropriate to mention them in the middle. Know this. End.

The matter concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[19] ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam. And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of jealous animosity among themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah – indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾

﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾ is a resumed sentence (jumlah mustaʾnafah) emphasizing the first, meaning: there is no religion acceptable to Allah, exalted is He, other than Islam, which is monotheism and adherence to the noble sharia (qalahu Abu al-Suʿud). And in the other verse: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers﴾ [Al ʿImran: 85].

﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ﴾ absolutely, or the Jews specifically, regarding the religion of (p-812) Islam: ﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾, meaning: only after they had come to know that it is the truth from which there is no turning away. Their disagreement was not due to any doubt they had, but rather: ﴿out of jealous animosity among themselves﴾, meaning: envy existing among them, and seeking leadership. This is a condemnation of them upon a condemnation.

﴿And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah﴾ that were sent down: ﴿indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ stands in place of the answer of the conditional clause, and is its cause. That is: indeed, He, exalted is He, will requite him and punish him for his disbelief soon, for indeed He is swift in reckoning.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 20:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[20] ﴿And if they argue with you, say: "I have submitted myself entirely to God, and so have those who follow me." And say to those who were given the Book and to the unlettered: "Have you submitted?" If they submit, then they are guided; but if they turn away, then your duty is only to convey the message. And God is Seeing of [His] servants.﴾

﴿And if they argue with you﴾ concerning the religion and dispute with you about it after the establishment of those signs, ﴿then say: "I have submitted myself to God"﴾, meaning: I have yielded to His revealed signs, and I have made my self and my worship sincere for Him, associating none other with Him in them. Abu al-Su'ud said: He expressed the self by the face because it is the most noble of the outward limbs, the seat of the faculties and the senses, and the gathering place of most of what worship is performed by, such as prostration and recitation, and by it one turns toward everything. ﴿And those who follow me﴾ is a conjunction with the attached pronoun.

A subtle point:

Is His saying, ﴿So say: "I have submitted myself to God"﴾, a turning away from argument, or is it itself an argument and a display of proof? Those who hold the first view reason that the Prophet ﷺ had already displayed to them the proof of his truthfulness before the revelation of this verse, many times and in various ways, for this surah is Medinan, and he had shown them many miracles through the Qur'an and other things. After this he said: ﴿And if they argue with you, say: "I have submitted"﴾, etc. That is: we have gone to great lengths in establishing the proofs and clarifying the evidences; if you abandon arrogance and envy and hold fast to them, you will be guided. But if you turn away, then God is behind your recompense. This interpretation is a common way of speaking. For when the righteous one is tested by the stubborn falsifier, and presents him with proof repeatedly, he may say at the end: "As for me and those who follow me, we are submissive to the truth, yielding to it, devoting ourselves to the worship of God Most High. If you agree and follow the truth that I am upon after these proofs I have mentioned, you are guided; but if you turn away, God is on the watch."

This is a method that the righteous arguer may mention to the obstinate falsifier at the end of his speech. Those who hold the second view, namely that it is an argument, mention in the manner of the inference from it what Abu Muslim al-Isfahani mentioned: that the Jews, the Christians, and the idol-worshippers all acknowledged the exalted status of Abraham, peace and blessings be upon him, and admitted that he was truthful in his speech and sincere in his religion. God therefore commanded Muhammad ﷺ to follow his creed, saying: ﴿Then We revealed to you: follow the religion of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [al-Nahl: 123]. Then God commanded Muhammad ﷺ in this passage to say what Abraham said, when he said: ﴿Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, as a man of pure faith, and I am not of the polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 79]. So Muhammad's saying ﴿I have submitted my face﴾ is like Abraham's saying, peace be upon him: ﴿I have turned my face﴾ [al-An'am: 79], meaning: I have turned away from every object of worship other than God Most High, directed my worship to Him, and devoted myself sincerely to Him. The sense of the verse is as if God Most High had said: "If they dispute with you, O Muhammad, in these details, say: I hold fast to the way of Abraham, and you acknowledge that his way is true, far from any doubt or accusation." This is then of the kind of holding to what the opponent is committed to, and falls under His saying: ﴿And argue with them in the best manner﴾ [al-Nahl: 125]. (Related by al-Razi.)

﴿And say to those who were given the Book and to the unlettered﴾, that is, those who have no Book, like the idolaters of the Arabs: ﴿Have you submitted?﴾ to these signs as I have submitted, or are you still upon disbelief? al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning is that there has come to you from the clear proofs what necessitates submission and requires its occurrence without doubt. So have you submitted, or are you still upon your disbelief? This is like your saying to one to whom you have summarized a matter, leaving no path of explanation and clarification unexplored: "Did you understand it?" And of the same kind is His saying, Mighty and Exalted: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 91], after mentioning the deterrents from wine and gambling. In this question there is a reproach, a rebuke for stubbornness and lack of fairness, for the fair-minded person, when the proof becomes clear to him, does not hesitate to submit to the truth, whereas for the stubborn one, after the proof has become clear, there is something that places barriers between him and submission. Likewise in "Did you understand it?" there is a rebuke for dullness and lack of aptitude. And in ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 91] there is a rebuke for holding back from desisting and for keen eagerness to engage in what is forbidden. End.

﴿If they submit, then they are guided﴾, that is, they have come out of error and benefited themselves. ﴿But if they turn away﴾ from your guidance and direction, ﴿then your duty is only to convey the message﴾, that is, to convey the signs of God, not to compel them when they oppose you, since their guidance is not your responsibility. ﴿And God is Seeing of [His] servants﴾: a promise and a warning.

Ibn Kathir said: This verse and its like are among the clearest indications of the universality of the mission of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, to all creation, as is known necessarily from his religion, and as the Book and the Sunnah indicate in many verses and hadiths. Among that is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O people, I am the Messenger of God to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1]. In the two Sahihs and others, and by multiple incidents whose transmission is established by consensus, he ﷺ sent his letters calling the kings of the horizons and the peoples of the children of Adam, from their Arabs and non-Arabs, their People of the Book and their unlettered, in compliance with God's command to him in this. 'Abd al-Razzaq related from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is! No one from this community hears of me, be he Jew or Christian, and dies without believing in what I was sent with, except that he will be among the people of the Fire." Related by Muslim. And he ﷺ said: "I was sent to the red and the black." And he said: "A prophet used to be sent to his own people specifically, but I was sent to mankind generally." And other verses and hadiths besides these.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[21] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people, give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people﴾ are the Jews. They killed Zakariyya and his son Yahya, peace be upon them both, and they killed Ḥizqīl (Ezekiel), peace be upon him. He was killed by a Jewish judge when he forbade him from an evil that he had committed. They also claimed that they killed ʿĪsā ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary), peace be upon them both. Since those addressed were content with the deeds of their forefathers, this attribution to them was valid. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿without right﴾, indicates that their killing of the prophets was without right, also in their own belief, so it is more emphatic in censure of them: ﴿so give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[22] ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.﴾

﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter﴾ means that their deeds, the righteous and good works they performed, have been nullified in both abodes. As for this world, it is the replacement of praise with blame, and of commendation with cursing and disgrace. This includes what befalls them of killing, captivity, the seizure of their property as spoils of war, their enslavement, and other humiliation and evident abasement among them. As for its voiding in the Hereafter, it is the replacement of reward with painful punishment. ﴿And they will have no helpers﴾ means no one who will help them against the punishment of Allah. The verse indicates the great standing of one who enjoins what is good, and the enormity of the sin of the one who kills him, since it joined that with disbelief in Allah and the killing of prophets.

Al-Hakim said: It indicates the correctness of what has been said, that one should enjoin what is good even if he fears for himself, and that this is preferable because of what it contains of strengthening the religion. Thus in the hadith: "The best jihad is a word of truth before an unjust ruler."

(p-818)

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[23] ﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They are invited to the Book of Allah that it may judge between them; then a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing.﴾

﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾ That is, the Torah. What is meant by them are the rabbis (aḥbār) of the Jews. ﴿They are invited to the Book of Allah﴾ which is the Qur'an. ﴿That it may judge between them; then a faction of them turns away﴾ is an expression of astonishment at their turning away after their knowledge that returning to the Book of Allah is obligatory, since the proofs indicating its revelation had been established against them. ﴿While they are refusing﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to "a faction," meaning: refusing to accept its judgment. Or it is a parenthetical clause (i‘tirāḍ), meaning: they are a people whose habit is turning away from the truth and persisting in falsehood. Among the exegetes, there are those who understood His saying ﴿They are invited to the Book of Allah﴾ to refer to the Torah, and that the verse alludes to the story of the Jews bringing their dispute to the Prophet ﷺ when two of them had committed adultery, and he ruled that they be stoned. They refused and said: "We do not find in our Book anything but the tahmīm (blackening of the face)." The Torah was brought, and stoning was found in it, so they were stoned, and they became angry, so he censured them with this verse. And Allah knows best.

Some of the exegetes said: The verse has two fruits (benefits):

The first: Whoever is invited to the Book of Allah and to what it contains of the law, it is obligatory upon him to respond. The scholars, may Allah be pleased with them, have said: It is recommended that he say "We hear and we obey" (samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan), based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The only statement of the believers, when they are invited to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey." And those will be the successful.﴾ [al-Nūr: 51]

The second fruit: Islam is not a condition for ihṣān (marital chastity), because the Prophet ﷺ stoned the two Jews, and the verse came confirming that. End of quote. That is, according to this view, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 24:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[24] ﴿That is because they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days." And their forgery deceived them in their religion.﴾

﴿That﴾ refers to the turning away and aversion. ﴿Because they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days"﴾, meaning: because of their making light of the matter of punishment for themselves. ﴿And their forgery deceived them in their religion﴾ refers to what they were fabricating in their saying that. In the expression "deception" (ghurur) and "fabrication" (iftira') there is an indication that what they told themselves and made easy for themselves is a pretext based on falsehood and a craving for what cannot be. Then He rejected their stated saying and nullified what had deceived them, by magnifying and dramatizing what He has prepared for them, and that they will fall into what they have no means of averting, with His saying:

The commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[25] ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full what it has earned, while they will not be wronged?﴾

﴿So how﴾ will they act, and how will their condition be? ﴿When We gather them for a Day﴾, i.e., on a day (p-820) ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾, i.e., no uncertainty, and it is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And every soul will be paid in full what it has earned﴾, i.e., the recompense of what it did of good or evil. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾: the pronoun refers to "every soul" according to its meaning, because it carries the sense of "every person." That is, they will not be wronged by an increase in punishment or a reduction in reward. Then the Exalted taught His Prophet (ﷺ) how to supplicate to Him and glorify Him by His saying:

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:**

[26] ﴿Say: "O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will, and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You exalt whom You will, and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent."﴾

﴿Say: "O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty"﴾ means: the Owner of the category of sovereignty absolutely, a true ownership by which You dispose of it as You will, by bringing into being and annihilating, giving life and causing death, punishing and rewarding, without any partner or any one to prevent You.

﴿You give sovereignty to whom You will﴾ is an explanation of some of the aspects of disposal that the ownership of sovereignty requires, and a confirmation that ownership belongs to Him, Exalted is He, in reality, while the ownership of others is by way of metaphor. This is indicated by the preference for (ita', giving), which is merely bestowal, over (tamlik, making someone an owner), which indicates the establishment of ownership in reality. This was stated by Abu al-Su'ud.

The use of (man, whoever), which is general for rational beings, in the expression implies that sovereignty may be attained by one who was not of its people. The people furthest from it were the Arabs. Thus it implies that Allah bestows the sovereignty of Persia and Rome upon the Arabs, as indeed happened, and that what remains will end with those who attained sovereignty through them and relied upon them, from the rest of the nations who entered this Ummah, from the tribes of the non-Arabs and the various peoples of the regions, until the matter reaches the point where Allah strips all the people of the earth of sovereignty with the manifestation of the sovereignty of the Day of Religion. So said al-Biqa'i:

﴿And You take sovereignty away from whom You will, and You exalt whom You will, and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.﴾

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[27] ﴿You cause the night to enter into the day, and You cause the day to enter into the night, and You bring the living out of the dead, and You bring the dead out of the living, and You provide for whom You will without account.﴾

﴿You cause the night to enter into the day and You cause the day to enter into the night﴾ means: You cause each of them to enter into the other, either by succession or by increase and decrease. ﴿And You bring the living out of the dead and You bring the dead out of the living﴾ refers to such things as an animal coming out of sperm drops and sperm drops coming out of an animal, and an egg coming out of a bird and the reverse. It has also been said that it means bringing a believer out of an unbeliever and the reverse. Al-Qaffal (al-Qaffal) said: The expression admits of all of these. As for unbelief and faith, God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life﴾ (al-An'am: 122), meaning: one who was an unbeliever and We guided him. So He made death to be unbelief and life to be faith. He also called the bringing forth of plants from the earth "giving life," and He called the earth dead before that, saying: ﴿He gives life to the earth after its death﴾ (al-Rum: 50), and He said: ﴿Then We drive it to a dead land and give life thereby to the earth after its death﴾ (Fatir: 9), and He said: ﴿How can you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life, then He causes you to die, then He gives you life, then to Him you will be returned?﴾ (al-Baqarah: 28). ﴿And You provide for whom You will without account﴾ means: abundant provision, unlimited.(p-822)

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies (awliya') instead of the believers. And whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah, except when you fear a danger from them. And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the final return.﴾

﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies (awliya')﴾: awliya' is the plural of walī, which has many meanings, among them: the lover, the friend, and the helper. Al-Zamakhshari said: They were forbidden to befriend the disbelievers because of kinship between them, or friendship before Islam, or other such causes by which people become close friends and companions. This is repeated in the Qur'an: ﴿Whoever among you takes them as allies, then he is indeed one of them﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 51]; ﴿Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 51]; ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah...﴾ [al-Mujadila: 22], and so on. Love for the sake of Allah and hatred for the sake of Allah is a great principle and one of the foundations of faith.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿instead of the believers﴾ (min dun al-mu'minin) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). That is: going beyond the believers toward them, either exclusively or jointly. In this is an indication that the believers are the most deserving of friendship, and that in their friendship there is a sufficient alternative to friendship with the disbelievers.

﴿And whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah﴾: that is, whoever allies with the disbelievers has no share at all in the allegiance (wilaya) of Allah to which the name of wilaya applies. The meaning is that he has completely severed himself from the wilaya of Allah. This is a matter of reason, for allegiance to an ally and allegiance to his enemy are mutually incompatible. He said:

"You love my enemy, then you claim that you are my friend; the folly is not far from you."

Al-Zamakhshari cited this.

﴿except when you fear a danger from them (illa an tattaqū minhum tuqāh)﴾: that is, you fear from them something to be feared. So you show allegiance to them with the tongue, not the heart, to ward off harm, as al-Bukhari reported from Abu al-Darda', who said: "Indeed we smile in the faces of some people while our hearts curse them." The origin of tuqāh is wuqyah; the waw was replaced by a tā' as in tukhmah and tuhmah, and the yā' was changed to an alif. In al-Muhkam: tuqāh may be a verbal noun (maṣdar) or a plural; the verbal noun is preferable, because in the other reading it is tuqyah.

Note:

Some of the Zaydi exegetes said: The fruit of this noble verse is the prohibition of allying with the disbelievers, because Allah the Exalted forbade it by His saying: ﴿whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah﴾. Then He excepted taqiyya and permitted allegiance to them for its sake, so outward companionship is permitted while the heart is at peace with enmity toward them and hatred, awaiting the removal of the obstacle. Al-Hakim said: The verse indicates the permissibility of showing reverence to oppressors to guard against their evil. He said: This is only appropriate through allusions that are not lies. Al-Sadiq said: Taqiyya is obligatory; I hear a man in the mosque cursing me and I hide from him behind the pillar so that he does not see me. From al-Hasan: taqiyya with the tongue, while the heart is at peace with faith.

Know that allegiance, which is intimacy, consultation, and disclosure of secrets to the disbelievers, is not permitted. If it is said: many scholars have permitted marriage to a disbelieving woman, and in that there is considerable mixing and intimacy with the woman that is no secret — the answer to that is: the intended meaning is allegiance in matters of religion, and in what involves honoring them. If it is said: concerning the occasion of revelation of the verse, that the Prophet ﷺ forbade ʿUbada ibn al-Samit from seeking the help of the Jews against Quraysh; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made an alliance with the Jews against the war with Quraysh, and in this is evidence of the permissibility of seeking their help. Al-Radi billah mentioned that it is permitted to seek the help of sinners against the war of the wrongdoers. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made an alliance with the Jews against Quraysh and others, until they broke it on the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). And the Prophet ﷺ set the alliance between himself and Khuza'a. Al-Radi billah said: This is well-known from our forefathers, peace be upon them, and ʿAli, peace be upon him, sought help from the murderers of ʿUthman. Perhaps the answer — and Allah knows best — is that seeking help is permitted when there is need for it. The seeking of help by the Messenger ﷺ from the Jews is to be understood in this sense. It is forbidden when there is no need, or when there is fear of harm from them. On this basis is to be understood the hadith of ʿUbada ibn al-Samit. Thus the forbidden allegiance occurs through inner enmity toward the believers and affection for the disbelievers in their disbelief; there is no ambiguity in its prohibition and no exception applies to it. Allegiance through showing honor, good companionship and friendship through disclosing secrets and the like — there is no ambiguity in its prohibition either, and no exception applies to it. Allegiance through showing honor, good companionship and consultation in what does not harm the Muslims. The apparent sense of al-Zamakhshari's words is that it is not permitted except for taqiyya. From this it follows that whoever allies with a disbeliever or a sinner is disobedient, but how far does his disobedience extend? This requires detail: if allegiance means affection, namely that he loves him for his disobedience, that is like contentment with disobedience. If the allegiance amounts to disbelief, he disbelieves. If it amounts to sin, he sins. If it entails neither disbelief nor sin, he neither disbelieves nor sins. If allegiance means alliance and support: if it is an alliance on a matter that is permissible or obligatory, such as the believers repelling from the People of the Covenant whoever harasses them and agreeing with them on that, there is no blame in it; indeed it is obligatory. If it is an alliance on a forbidden matter, such as agreeing with them to seize the wealth of the Muslims and to dominate them, this is disobedience beyond doubt. Likewise if it means that he reveals the secret of the Muslims and loves the safety of the disbelievers, not because of their disbelief but because of a favor they did him or kinship or the like, this is disobedience beyond doubt. But it does not reach the level of disbelief, because it is not reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ declared Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a a disbeliever.

Al-Radi billah said: Supporting the disbelievers against the Muslims makes one a disbeliever, because the Prophet ﷺ said to al-Abbas: "He supported you against us." He excused himself on the ground that he went out under compulsion. As for mere kindness to a disbeliever, it is permissible, provided it is not to seek his help against the Muslims or merely to make him comfortable. Likewise, if one feels constrained by his distress in a specific matter for a permissible purpose, it is permissible, as when the Muslims were distressed by the victory of the Persians over the Romans. The conclusion of the school is that the allegiance that makes one a disbeliever is that the allegiant agrees to disbelief, and the allegiance that makes one a sinner is that he agrees to sin. If it is asked: what is the ruling on one who enlists with the oppressors so that they may use him for taxes and kinds of injustice? We say: he is disobedient beyond doubt, and a sinner beyond doubt, because he has become one of them, and their sinfulness is known. If it is asked: what if he enlists with them to fight the imam of the Muslims? We say: he has become a rebel, and his sinfulness arises from rebellion and injustice. If it is asked: it is related from al-Mahdi ʿAli ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, that he declared apostate whoever enlisted with the sultan of Yemen and ruled for his apostasy; we say: this requires explanation of the grounds for takfir by a decisive proof. And if it is permissible to say that this is a term for the matter of the imam, just as al-Hadi, peace be upon him, rejected the testimony of one who refused to give allegiance to the imam, then that would be a possibility. — End of his words, may Allah have mercy on him.

From this verse the scholars derived the legitimacy of taqiyya under fear. Al-Murtada al-Yamani reported consensus on its permissibility in that situation in his book (Ithar al-Haqq ʿala al-Khalq), where he said the following text:

"Two matters increase the truth's obscurity and concealment: First, the fear of the knowers, though few, from scholars of evil, sultans of tyranny, and devils among people, while taqiyya at such times is permitted by the explicit text of the Qur'an and the consensus of the people of Islam. Fear has always prevented the manifestation of truth, and the one who upholds the truth has never ceased to be an enemy to most people. It is authentically reported from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that in that early era he said: 'I memorized two vessels from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. As for one of them, I spread it among the people; as for the other, if I spread it, this throat would be cut.' The matter continued to grow worse. Al-Ghazali clearly stated this in the preface of (al-Maqsad al-Asna) and hinted at his opposition to his companions in it, as he stated in the commentary on (al-Rahman al-Rahim). He affirmed the wisdom and mercy of Allah and expounded on that, thinking that they would not understand the opposition, because the explanation of these two names is not the place of this question; therefore he set it aside and turned away from it in its proper place, which is the name of the Harmful (al-Darr), as the intelligent scholars know."

Al-Juwayni pointed to taqiyya in the introductions of (al-Burhan) on the question of the eternity of the Qur'an, and al-Razi in his book called (al-Arba'in fi Usul al-Din), to the end of what al-Murtada cited; consult it.

﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾: that is, of His holy essence, so do not expose yourselves to His wrath by opposing His rulings and allying with His enemies. This is a great warning indicating the extreme ugliness of what is forbidden. He mentioned "Himself" so that it may be known that what is to be feared is a punishment proceeding from Him, the Exalted; so one should not be concerned with what is to be feared from the disbelievers beside Him. ﴿And to Allah is the final return﴾: that is, the place of return and the destination, that He may recompense every doer for his deed.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[29] ﴿Say: "Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it. And He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. And Allah is over all things competent."﴾

This is a warning. And it intends the concealing of the disbelievers' affection and their allegiance, and their displaying of it; or the denial of the Prophet (ﷺ); or disbelief. In this verse there is an admonition from Him, exalted is He, to His servants regarding His vigilance and His watchfulness, so that they do not commit what He has forbidden. For He is Knowing of all their affairs and Able to hasten their punishment, and even if He gives respite to whoever He gives respite among them, He grants them time and then seizes them with the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. For this reason He said after this:

(p-828)

"The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[30] ﴿On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that were a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants.﴾

﴿On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present﴾ — either in forms suited to it, or in the scrolls of the angels. Or the meaning is: the recompense of what it has done. (And) ﴿will find﴾ — "what it has done of evil" [is the object of "will find," and] ﴿it will wish that between it and that were a great distance﴾ — i.e., its evil deed: ﴿a great distance﴾, meaning a far-off limit such that neither reaches the other. And ﴿will wish﴾ is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). The estimated sense is: "it will find what it has done of evil present, while wishing that." ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾ — He repeated it so that it would be in your minds, not something you neglect. Thus (it is stated) in al-Kashshaf.

Abu al-Su'ud said: It is a repetition of what preceded and a restatement of it, but not for emphasis alone; rather, to convey what the phrase ﴿and Allah is Kind to the servants﴾ conveys, namely that His warning of them stems from His kindness toward them and His vast mercy, or that His kindness toward them does not prevent the realization of what He has warned them of concerning His punishment, and that His warning is not based on forgetting the attribute of kindness, but rather exists alongside its reality."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 31:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He:

[31] ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Ibn Kathir said: This noble verse is decisive against everyone who claims the love of Allah while not being upon the Muhammadan way. Indeed, he is a liar in that claim until he follows the Muhammadan Law in all his sayings and actions, as it is established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected."

(p-829)

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted be He:

[32] ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger. But if they turn away, then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers.﴾

﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger. But if they turn away﴾: they turned away from obedience. ﴿then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers.﴾

The discussion of God's words:

[33] ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran over the worlds.﴾

﴿Indeed, Allah chose﴾ means: He selected by means of prophethood (nubuwwah). ﴿Adam﴾: He created him with His own hand, breathed into him of His spirit, taught him the names of all things, settled him in the Garden, and then sent him down from it, for reasons of wisdom that He had regarding that. (And) He chose (and) ﴿Noah﴾: He made him the first messenger to the people of the earth, when the people worshipped idols and associated with Allah what He had not sent down any authority for. He saved those who followed him in the Ark and drowned those who disobeyed him. (And) He chose ﴿the family of Abraham﴾ [An-Nisa: 54], meaning his kinsmen and close relatives, namely Isma'il, Isḥaq, and the prophets from their descendants, among whom is the Prophet (ﷺ). As for the choosing of Abraham himself, peace be upon him, it is understood from the choosing of his family by way of priority. The fact that it is not explicitly stated is to indicate that it is unnecessary to mention it, because the matter of his intimate friendship (al-khullah) is so well known, and because he was the leader of the prophets and the exemplar of the messengers, peace be upon them all, and because the choosing of his family came through his supplication in His words: ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 129], and so on. For this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "I am the answer to the supplication of my father Abraham." (And) He chose: ﴿the family of Imran﴾, since He placed among them ʿIsa, peace be upon him, who was given the clear signs (al-bayyinat) and was strengthened with the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus). The Imran intended here is the father of Maryam, mother of ʿIsa, peace be upon them both. ﴿Over the worlds﴾ means: over the worlds of their times. That is: (p-830) He chose each one of them over the worlds of his own time. Al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: This verse is used as evidence for the superiority of the prophets over the angels, since the prophets are included among "the worlds."

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[34] ﴿Offspring, one of another. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

﴿Offspring﴾ means progeny. It is in the accusative either as a substitute (badal) for the two families, or as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of them.

A subtle point:

The word dhurriyyah (ذُرِّيَّة) may be vocalized in three ways, and it is only heard without hamza. It is a term for the offspring of the two species (jinn and humankind). It may also be applied to ancestors and origins. God Almighty says: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾ [Ya-Sin: 41].

Al-Saghani said: As for its derivation, there are two views. The first is that it comes from dhara'a (to create, produce), and its form is fu'ulah or fi'ilah. The second is that it comes from dharr meaning scattering, because God scattered them in the earth; its form is also fi'ilah or fu'ulah. Its original form is dharurah, and the third radical, the rāʾ, was changed to a yāʾ, as in taqaddat al-iqab. This is as stated in al-Qamus and its commentary.

﴿One of another﴾ is in the accusative position, as it is an attribute (sifah) of dhurriyyah. That is: He chose the two families, being offspring linked in succession, one from another, in the inheritance of chosen status. ﴿And Allah is Hearing﴾ of the sayings of the servants, ﴿Knowing﴾ of their inner thoughts and their deeds. He chooses from His creation only those whom He knows to be upright in word and deed. A parallel to this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and call upon Us in hope and fear, and they were humbly submissive to Us﴾ [al-Anbiya': 90].

**On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

[35] ﴿When the wife of ʿImran said: "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated one, so accept it from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing."﴾

﴿When the wife of ʿImran said⁠﴾ is in the accusative position as an object (*mafʿūliyyah*), governed by a verb implied in the sense of a new sentence (*ʿalā ṭarīqat al-istiʾnāf*, as a resumptive clause), to establish the choosing of the family of ʿImran and to explain how it occurred. That is: "Mention to them the time when she said..." etc. The wife of ʿImran here is the mother of Mary, upon her be peace.

**Benefit:**

The scholar al-Nuwayri said in *Ghayth al-Nafʿ*: "*Imra'at ʿImran* is written with a *tāʾ* (ت). Every instance of the word *imraʾah* in the Book of God, may His remembrance be exalted, is written with a *hāʾ* (ه), and there are seven places: this first one; the second and third in Yusuf, ﴿the wife of the ʿAziz is seeking to seduce⁠﴾ [Yusuf: 30], ﴿now the wife of the ʿAziz⁠﴾ [Yusuf: 51]; the fourth in al-Qasas, ﴿the wife of Pharaoh⁠﴾ [al-Qasas: 9]; and the fifth, sixth and seventh in al-Tahrim, ﴿the wife of Noah⁠﴾ [al-Tahrim: 10], ﴿and the wife of Lot⁠﴾ [al-Tahrim: 10], and ﴿the wife of Pharaoh⁠﴾ [al-Tahrim: 11]. So if one pauses on it, al-Makki and the two grammarians (*al-naḥwiyyān*) pause with a *hāʾ*, and the rest pause with a *tāʾ*." End of quotation.

﴿My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated one⁠﴾ meaning: devoted (*mukhlaṣan*) to worship, according to al-Shaʿbi. Or a servant who serves in Your places of worship; *ḥarrarahu* means he made him a devoted one in the service of the sanctuary for as long as he lives, and he is not permitted to abandon it in his religion, according to al-Zajjaj. The verse indicates the validity of a mother's vow concerning her child, and that a mother may benefit from a young child for her own needs; therefore she made him belong to another. The meaning is: I have vowed him as a endowment (*waqf*) for Your obedience, and I shall not occupy him with any of my affairs.

Abu Mansur said in *al-Taʾwilat*: She made what was in her womb purely for God, not seeking from him companionship or what people hope for from their children. This is from the chosen ones whom He, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned. Likewise, it is obligatory for everyone who seeks a child to seek it for the same purpose for which the wife of ʿImran and Zakariyya sought it, when he said: ﴿My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring⁠﴾ [Al ʿImran: 38], and as Ibrahim asked: ﴿My Lord, grant me of the righteous⁠﴾ [al-Saffat: 100], and as in His saying: ﴿And those who say: "Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort to our eyes, and make us leaders for the righteous⁠﴾ [al-Furqan: 74]. Thus it is obligatory that a child be sought in this manner, not for the sake of companionship, support, or help in livelihood. End of quotation.

﴿So accept it from me, indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing⁠﴾ meaning: accept from me my offering and what I have dedicated to You purely for You. *Taqabbul* means taking something in a manner of approval.

[p. 834] The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[36] ﴿So when she gave birth to her, she said, "My Lord, I have given birth to a female," and God knows best what she gave birth to. "The male is not like the female. I have named her Maryam, and I seek refuge for her in You, and for her offspring, from the accursed Satan."﴾

﴿When she gave birth to her﴾: the pronoun refers to "what is in my womb." It is feminine because of the sense of the word, since what was in her womb was female in God's knowledge. Alternatively, it is feminine because of the interpretation of "soul" (nafs) or "breath" (nasamah). ﴿She said, "My Lord, I have given birth to a female"﴾: that is, I had hoped it would be a male. She expressed regret or made an apology because she did not know its true worth. ﴿And God knows best what she gave birth to﴾: it is read in the seven canonical readings with the ta' (ت) both sukun and damma. On the first reading, the parenthetical clause is part of God's own speech, either to dispel what might appear to be the case, namely that her saying "My Lord, I have given birth to a female" was intended to inform God, who has no need to be informed, so the doubt is removed by His saying "God knows best what she gave birth to." This is what appears to me. Or, it is as they have mentioned, that the parenthetical clause (al-i'tiraad) is an exaltation from Him, exalted is He, of her offspring, a glorification of its status, and a notification to her of its worth. That is: God knows best the soul she gave birth to and what great matters were attached to it, and that He made her and her son a sign for the worlds, while she was unaware of this. On the second reading, namely with the damma on the ta', the parenthetical clause is part of her speech. This is either for the first of the two previous aspects, as I have inclined to, or for what they have mentioned, that she intended an apology to God, exalted is He, since she had brought forth a child not suited to what she had vowed, or a consolation for herself, in the sense of: perhaps God has a secret and wisdom in it, and perhaps this female is better than a male. ﴿And the male is not like the female﴾: this is also a parenthetical clause. It is either from God's speech, intended as an excuse for her regret and grief, by explaining the superiority of the male over the female. This is why souls are naturally inclined to desire the male rather than the female, especially in this situation, namely the situation of intending to devote the vowed child to worship. The male surpasses the female in several respects:

Among them: the male is able to continue serving the place of worship, whereas this is not valid for the female because of menstruation and the other conditions of women.

Among them: the male is suited, by his strength and vigor, to service, unlike the female, who is weak and unable to bear service.

Among them: the male does not incur a defect in service or in mixing with people, whereas the female does.

Among them: the male does not incur the suspicion during mixing that the female incurs.

These aspects require the superiority of the male over the female in this situation. The lam in "the male" and "the female" according to this interpretation is the lam of genus (lam al-jins), as it appeared to me. According to their saying that the lam is the lam of anaphora (lam al-'ahd) in both: that is, the male is not the one she requested and imagined to be perfect, whose highest attainment would be to be one of the rabbis, like the female who was given to her. For the circle of her knowledge and her hope hardly encompasses what is in it of grand matters. This is one view. Alternatively, this sentence may be part of her speech, and the purpose then is to strengthen the apology by explaining that the male is not like the female in virtue, excellence, and suitability for service in places of worship, since they are far removed from that.

Thus the lam is the lam of genus.

A subtle point:
It has been said: the analogy, if it is from her speech, would be "the female is not like the male," since her intention is to belittle the female in comparison with the male. The usual practice in such a case is to deny to the deficient the resemblance to the perfect, not the reverse. Al-Nasir said in al-Intisaf: The matter has been found to differ in this, and so what has been said is not established. Do you not see His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You are not like any of the women﴾ [al-Ahzab: 32], where He denied the resemblance of the deficient to the perfect, although the perfection of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) is established in relation to women in general. In this same manner came the expression "the wife of 'Imran." And God knows best. Also from this is His saying: ﴿Is one who creates like one who does not create? Will you not then remember?﴾ [al-Nahl: 17]. End of quotation.

﴿And I have named her Maryam﴾: the exegetes said: in their language it means "the worshipper." She named her thus, hoping and taking it as a good omen, that her deed would correspond to her name.
