However, I have seen in the interpretation of the names found in the Torah and the Gospel that Maryam means "bitterness" or "the bitter of the sea." So let it be examined. Al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: In the verse there is evidence for the permissibility of naming children on the day of birth, and that it is not restricted to the seventh day, because she said this immediately upon the birth. Also in it is the legitimacy of the mother naming the child, and that this is not exclusive to the father. Then she sought its protection, saying: ﴿And I seek refuge for her in You﴾, that is: I ask You to grant her protection by Your guarding. ﴿And her offspring from the accursed Satan﴾, that is: the one expelled because of his opposition to You. So do not give him any authority over her or her offspring that would be a cause of their being expelled.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 37:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[37] ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance and caused her to grow up in a goodly growth, and He entrusted her to Zechariah. Every time Zechariah entered upon her in the sanctuary (mihrab), he found with her provision. He said, "O Mary, from where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."﴾

﴿So her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance﴾ — that is, He received her, or took charge of her. He did not say "with a goodly receiving" (bi-taqabbul), so as to combine both matters: the taqabbul (receiving), which is the progression in acceptance, and the qabul (acceptance), which entails approval and reward. Al-Mahayimi said: "With a goodly acceptance, He made her above many of the saints," ﴿and caused her to grow up in a goodly growth﴾ by making her offspring among the great prophets. — End quote. Al-Zamakhshari said: Her "growth" is a metaphor for the goodly upbringing that returns to her, by which she is made righteous in all her circumstances, i.e., in righteousness, rectitude, chastity and obedience. ﴿And He entrusted her to Zechariah﴾, that is, He gathered her to him; it was also read with the doubled letter (kaffala, with shaddah). Zechariah is in the accusative, whether written defectively or with the long vowel, and the agent is Allah. That is, He made him her guardian, responsible for her welfare, and in charge of managing her affairs. It has been narrated that her mother took her and carried her to the mosque, and placed her with the rabbis, saying: "Take this consecrated offering (nadhirah)," and they competed for her, since she was the daughter of their leader and the keeper of their offerings, and each wished to obtain the honor of raising her. Zechariah said to them: "I have the greatest right to her, since her maternal aunt is with me." But they refused except by lot, and they went off to a river and cast their pens into it, on the condition that whoever's pen remained in the water and rose up would have the greater right to her. Zechariah's pen floated, and theirs sank. To this refers His saying, exalted is He, in another verse: ﴿When they cast their pens, which of them would take charge of Mary﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44]. Zechariah took her and raised her in the lap of her aunt. When she grew up and reached the age of women, she withdrew into her sanctuary (mihrab), worshipping therein, and reached the state in which: ﴿Every time Zechariah entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found with her provision. He said, "O Mary, from where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."﴾

Among the issues of the verse:

The first: On the meaning of al-mihrab. In the Qamus and its commentary, the text reads: "Al-mihrab: the upper room and the high place," transmitted by al-Harawi in his Gharib from al-Asma'i. Wadah al-Yaman said:

"The mistress of a mihrab: when I came to her I did not reach her, nor did I climb a ladder."

Abu 'Ubaydah said: The mihrab is the chief, the foremost and most honored of the assemblies, and so it is of the mosques. (p-837) From al-Asma'i: the Arabs call a palace a mihrab because of its nobility. Al-Azhari said: The mihrab, as the common people understand it, is the standing place of the imam in the mosque. Ibn al-Anbari said: It was called the mihrab of the mosque because the imam is alone in it and distant from the people. From this one says: "So-and-so is a harb (enemy) to so-and-so," if there is distance and hostility between them. In al-Misbah: It is said to be derived from al-muharabah (warfare), because the one praying wages war against Satan and against his own self by presenting his heart. Then he said: The mihrabs of the Children of Israel are their mosques in which they used to sit. — End quote.

The second: The verse is evidence for the occurrence of karamah (miraculous favors) for the friends of Allah, exalted is He, as occurred with Khubayb ibn 'Adi al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, who was martyred in Makkah, when a cluster of grapes was found with him, as is in al-Bukhari. There are many parallels to this in the Book and the Sunnah. Among the subtle points here is what the Imam al-Sha'rani transmitted in (al-Yawaqit) from the gnostic Abu al-Hasan al-Shadhili, may his secret be sanctified, that he said: Mary, peace be upon her, was given knowledge of Allah in her beginnings by the breaking of customary norms without a cause, to strengthen her faith and perfect her certainty, so that every time Zechariah entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found provision with her. When her faith and certainty grew strong, she was returned to the means, since she did not stop at them, and it was said to her: ﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe dates﴾ [Maryam: 25]. — End quote.

The third: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah provides﴾ and so on, is an explanation of why it is from Allah. It is either part of her own speech, in which case it is in the accusative position, or it is from His own speech, exalted and majestic is He, in which case it is a new sentence. The meaning of ﴿without account﴾ is: without measure, due to its abundance; or without entitlement, by His bounty, exalted is He.

The fourth: The Zechariah mentioned here is the father of Yahya, peace be upon them both. The meaning of Zakariyya is "the remembrance of the Lord," as in the interpretation of the names in the Torah and the Gospel.

(p-838)

The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wil*) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[38] ﴿There Zechariah called upon his Lord. He said, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring. Indeed You are the Hearer of supplication."﴾

﴿There Zechariah called upon his Lord. He said, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring. Indeed You are the Hearer of supplication."﴾ This is a resumed statement and an independent narrative, which was introduced within the account of Mary, because of the strength of the connection between them and the close interweaving of the two, together with what its mention establishes of the purpose for which the account of Mary was related, namely the explanation of the choosing of the family of 'Imran. For the virtues of some relatives are evidence of the virtues of others. "There" (*hunā*) is an adverb of place, meaning: in that place, where he was with Mary in the sanctuary (*mihrab*). It may also be an adverb of time, meaning: at that time, since *hunā*, *thumma* and *haythu* are used metaphorically for time. Zechariah called upon his Lord when he saw the honour that Mary had with God and her station with Him, Exalted is He. He desired that he should have from his wife a child like the child of her sister in nobility and honour with God, Exalted is He, even though his wife was barren and aged, as stated in Abu al-Su'ud. "Offspring" (*dhurriyyah*) here means a child. Al-Zamakhshari said: it applies to the singular and the plural, and the discussion of it has already preceded shortly, at His saying: ﴿offspring, some of them from others﴾ [Al-'Imran: 34]. His saying ﴿good﴾ means: obedient to You, because that is the request of the people of special closeness (*al-khusus*), as has already been clarified in the verse: ﴿My Lord, I have vowed to You﴾ [Al-'Imran: 35], etc. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed You are the Hearer of supplication﴾ means: its Answerer. And the Truth, Exalted is He, answered him, so He sent to him the angels bearing good news, as Exalted is He said:

**The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

[39] ﴿Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: "Allah gives you good news of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah, and a master, chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous."﴾

﴿Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary, "Allah gives you good news﴾ meaning: through our tongues. ﴿of Yahya.﴾ It has been read in the seven canonical readings (al-Sab'ah) with a kasra and with a fatha on the *inna* (إنَّ). The name Yahya is an Arabized form (mu'arrab) of Yuhanna (يُوحَنّا), its name in Hebrew. The meaning of Yuhanna is "the grace of the Lord," as in the interpretation of the names in the Torah and the Gospel (Injil). ﴿Confirming a word from Allah﴾ meaning: a prophet created by the word "Be" (كُنْ) without a father. Allah sends him to His servants, and he confirms him. That is ʿIsa, peace be upon him. ﴿And a master﴾ meaning: he will lead his people and surpass them. ﴿And chaste﴾ meaning: he will not approach women, restraining himself from them, that is, preventing himself from desires out of chastity, asceticism, and devotion to obedience. ﴿And a prophet from among the righteous﴾ meaning: arising from them, because he is from their loins; or being one of their number, like His words: ﴿And indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous﴾ (al-Baqarah: 130).

When Zakariyya, peace be upon him, was certain of this good news, he began to marvel at the existence of a son from him after old age.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[40] ﴿He said, "My Lord, how can I have a boy when old age has already reached me and my wife is barren?" He said, "Thus does Allah do what He wills."﴾

﴿He said, "My Lord, how?"﴾ i.e., how, or from where: ﴿can I have a boy when old age has already reached me?﴾ i.e., complete old age has overtaken me, preventing childbearing and weakening me. ﴿And my wife is barren?﴾ i.e., she possesses ʿuqr (barrenness). It is of the form of nisba (a relative adjective), and in meaning it is passive, i.e., maʿqūrah (rendered barren). For this reason the feminine ending (tāʾ al-taʾnīth) was not attached. ﴿He said, "Thus"﴾, i.e., the child will be yours in the state in which you and your wife are, because Allah, exalted is He, does not need a cause. Rather, ﴿Allah does what He wills﴾; nothing overpowers Him and no matter is too great for Him.

Regarding the iʿrab (grammatical analysis) of ﴿thus﴾, there are several views. Among them: it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., the matter is thus, and His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Allah does what He wills﴾, is an explanation of it. Among them: the kāf is in the accusative position, on the basis that it is originally an adjective of an omitted verbal noun (maṣdar), i.e., Allah does what He wills with an act of that wondrous creation, which is the creation of a child from an aged old man and a barren old woman.

(p-840)

[41] Concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿He said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign." He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the morning."﴾

﴿He said﴾ — Zakariyya: ﴿"My Lord, appoint for me a sign"﴾ — that is, a token by which I may know that the pregnancy has taken place. He asked for it because conception is a hidden matter that cannot be ascertained, so he wanted God to inform him of it from its very beginning, so that he might receive that blessing with thanks from its first moments, and not delay it until it became manifest in the usual way. ﴿He said﴾ — God, exalted is He: ﴿"Your sign is that you will not speak to the people"﴾ — that is, that you will not be able to speak to them ﴿for three days except by gesture﴾ — that is, a signal with a hand or a head. Its being made his sign was so that the period would be devoted to the remembrance of God, exalted is He, in thanks for what He had bestowed upon him. It has also been said that this was a punishment from Him, exalted is He, because of his request for a sign after he had been addressed directly by the angels — related by al-Qurtubi from most of the exegetes. ﴿"And remember your Lord much"﴾ — that is, remembrance in abundance. ﴿"And glorify"﴾ — that is, and glorify Him: ﴿"in the evening"﴾, which is the end of the day. The word ʿashiyy (evening) is also applied to the period between midday and sunset. ﴿"and the morning"﴾ (al-ibkar), which is the early forenoon (al-ghadwa), or from the dawn prayer until the rising of the sun.

Al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: The verse contains an exhortation to the remembrance of God, exalted is He, which is among the branches of faith. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "If God had granted anyone a dispensation to abandon remembrance, He would have granted it to Zakariyya, for He prevented him from speech and commanded him to remember" — related by Ibn Abi Hatim.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[42] ﴿And when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds."﴾

﴿And when the angels said, "O Mary"﴾ is the beginning of the continuation of the virtues of the family of 'Imran. Al-Mahayimi said: In it is an indication of the permissibility of angels speaking to a walī (a saint or devoted servant of Allah), and it differs from a prophet in the claim of prophethood. ﴿Indeed Allah has chosen you﴾ by bringing you near and by love; ﴿and purified you﴾ from vices, so that your attraction to Him may endure; ﴿and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾ (p-841) by preference, and by what He manifested of His great power, in that He created from you a child without a father, which was not granted to any other woman. In al-Iklil: whoever held that Mary was a prophetess used this verse as evidence. Likewise, whoever preferred her over the daughters of the Prophet ﷺ and his wives used it as evidence. Its response: the intended meaning is the women of her own time, as said by al-Suddi.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[43] ﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, prostrate yourself, and bow with those who bow.﴾

﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾ means: worship Him in gratitude for His choosing you. ﴿And prostrate yourself and bow with those who bow﴾ means: so that you may increase in nearness (to Him) through much prostration and prayer. Al-Biqa'i said: "The apparent meaning here is that prostration is to be taken in its literal sense, and bowing (ruku') is the prayer itself. It is as if it were said: 'Prostrate yourself while praying, and let your prayer be with those who pray,' that is, in congregation, for you are among the men (in rank) because of the perfection with which you have been singled out." Then he said: "I have said this because I searched the Torah and did not find that it mentions bowing (ruku') in the prayer of Abraham or of the prophets after him, peace be upon them, nor of their followers, except in one place, where it cannot properly be taken in its literal sense. I found that it mentions prayer in it in three ways:

The first: the mention of the word for prayer without explanation of its manner.

The second: the mention of the word prostration on its own.

The third: its mention coupled with bowing, or kneeling, or falling on the face, and the like."

Then al-Biqa'i cited the texts that occur on this matter, and said afterwards: "What I have understood from these passages and others is that prayer, among them, is applied to supplication and to an act which is merely prostration. If there is mentioned along with it something that indicates placing the face upon the ground, then that is it, and in that case it is called prayer. Otherwise, what is meant by it is simply bowing down out of reverence. This agrees with the language, for in the Qamus (al-Qamus al-Muhit): sajada means 'to submit humbly,' and khudu' means 'to lower oneself.' As for the place in which bowing is mentioned, the apparent meaning is: the whole people performing prostration to God, because ruku' is used in the language with several meanings, among them prayer. It is said: raka'a, meaning 'he prayed,' and raka'a, meaning 'he bent down a great deal.' It is not valid to take ruku' in its literal sense there, because it cannot occur in the state of prostration; and even if a figurative interpretation were resorted to in it, it would not be a figurative interpretation like what I mentioned concerning ruku' — and God knows best. I relied on the language because the translator of the copy of the Torah that came into my hands is among the eloquent, as anyone who considers the places of his translation of it will know. Moreover, I asked about the prayer of the Jews today, and I was informed that there is no bowing (ruku') in it. Then I saw that al-Baghawi stated, in his commentary on the words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿And bow with those who bow﴾ [al-Baqarah: 43], that their prayer has no bowing in it; and likewise Ibn 'Atiyyah and others." End of al-Biqa'i's words.

A subtle point (lataifa):

al-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): The verse is evidence that congregational prayer is desired in prayer, and that for a woman congregational prayer is recommended.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 44:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[44] ﴿That is among the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them when they cast their pens (to decide) which of them would take charge of Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed.﴾

﴿That﴾ refers to what has preceded. ﴿Among the news of the unseen﴾ means: the news that is hidden from you. ﴿Which We reveal to you﴾ (conforming to what is in their Book). The pronoun in ﴿We reveal it﴾ is masculine, taking its referent to be ﴿That﴾. ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens, which of them would take charge of Mary﴾ means: you were not witnessing their action, nor what took place among them concerning Mary when they cast their pens (qalam, pl. aqlam), that is, their arrows, on which they had made marks by which it would be known who would take charge of Mary, by way of lot. ﴿Nor were you with them when they disputed﴾ over it, competing for her guardianship. It has been narrated from Qatadah and others that they went to the river Jordan and cast lots there, by casting their pens: whichever one remained fixed in the flow of the water would be her guardian. So they cast their pens, and the water carried them all away except the pen of Zakariyya, which remained fixed. It is said that it went upstream, cutting against the flow of the water, and God knows best.

Abu Muslim said: The meaning of ﴿they cast their pens﴾ is from what the nations used to do in drawing lots at disputes: they would throw in arrows on which they wrote their names, and whoever's arrow came out had the matter settled in his favor. God, exalted is He, has said: ﴿So he cast lots and was among the losers﴾ [al-Saffat: 141]. This is similar to the practice of the arrows by which the Arabs divided the meat of a slaughtered camel. These arrows were called pens (aqlam) because they are trimmed and shaped; whatever you cut from something bit by bit you have "qalamtahu," and for this reason what is written with is called a qalam. Al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: This verse is a basis for the use of lots in disputes. Some of the commentators of the Zaydiyyah said: The fruit of the verse is that it is permissible to dispute in seeking excellence, until one is distinguished by a merit, and it shows that distinction is achieved by lot in a case of ambiguity.

A subtle point:

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: why was witnessing negated, when its absence is known without doubt, while negating the hearing of the news from its memorizers was left out, though it is a mere supposition? I say: it was known to them with certain knowledge that he was not one of those who hear or read, and they were deniers of revelation, so only witnessing remained, and it is extremely far-fetched and impossible. So it was negated in the manner of mockery of those who deny revelation, while knowing that he had neither hearing nor reading. Similar to this: ﴿And you were not on the western side﴾ [al-Qasas: 44], ﴿And you were not on the side of Mount Sinai﴾ [al-Qasas: 46], ﴿And you were not with them when they resolved on their plan﴾ [Yusuf: 102]. End quote. In sum: the negation is an affirmation and confirmation that those news are revelation, in the manner of mockery toward those who deny it.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[45] ﴿When the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near."﴾

﴿When the angels said﴾ is the beginning of the account of Jesus, peace be upon him. ﴿O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him﴾ i.e., of a child who comes into being by a word from Him, without an intermediary father. ﴿Whose name﴾: He used the masculine pronoun referring back to "word" because it is an expression for a male. I.e., his name by which he is distinguished: as a title, ﴿the Messiah﴾, and as a proper name, ﴿Jesus﴾. It is an arabicized form of Yasu' (يسوع) with the unpointed sin, a Greek word meaning (savior), and its equivalent is Yashu' (يشوع) with the pointed shin, though it is Hebrew, as in the interpretation of the names in the Torah and the Gospel. It is also said that al-Masih means "the anointed" or "the one smeared with oil." Al-Biqa'i said: The origin of this description is that in their law, whoever was anointed by the imam with holy oil was pure, fit for kingship, knowledge and virtuous offices, and blessed. Thus Allah, glorified is He, indicated that Jesus, peace be upon him, is constantly associated with the blessing resulting from anointing, even though he was not anointed. End of quote. He said ﴿son of Mary﴾ although the address is to her, to draw attention to the fact that he is born without a father, so he is attributed only to his mother, and by this she was preferred over the women of the worlds. ﴿Distinguished in this world and the Hereafter﴾ i.e., honored and esteemed in both. ﴿And among those brought near﴾ i.e., near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

ON THE INTERPRETATION OF HIS SAYING, MIGHTY AND MAJESTIC IS HE:

[46] ﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and [he will be] among the righteous.﴾

﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). ﴿And in maturity﴾ is coordinated with it, in the sense of "and he will speak to the people," in the state of being a child and of being mature, speaking the speech of the prophets without any difference between the two states. Undoubtedly, this is an utmost sign of miraculousness (i'jāz). In this is also good news of his remaining alive until he becomes mature.

The mahd (cradle) is the place prepared and made comfortable for the infant to sleep in. The kahl (one in maturity) is one whom gray hair has touched, or who has passed thirty toward forty or fifty. Ibn al-A'rabi said: A boy is called murāhiq (adolescent), then muḥtalim (having reached puberty), then it is said: his face has come out (with the first hair), then his beard has become full, then mujtami' (fully grown), then kahl, and he is thirty-three years old. Al-Azhari said: He is called kahl at that time because his youth has ended and his strength is complete.

As for His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿and [he will be] among the righteous﴾, Ibn Jarir said: That is, from among their number and their allies, because the people of righteousness are among one another in religion and virtue.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[47] ﴿She said, "My Lord, how will I have a son when no man has touched me?" He said, "Thus Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is."﴾

﴿She said﴾, addressing Allah who sent the angels to her: ﴿My Lord, how will I have a son when no man has touched me?﴾ That is, "I am not one who has a husband." ﴿He said, "Thus"﴾ That is, in the state you are in, of no man having touched you: ﴿Allah creates what He wills﴾, and He has no need of a cause, and nothing can overpower Him. He stated here, "He creates what He wills," and did not say, "He does," as in the story of Zakariyya, because creating, which indicates bringing something into existence, is more fitting to this situation, so that no doubt remains for the one who would falsely argue. He emphasized this with His saying:

﴿When He decrees a matter﴾ among affairs, that is, when He wills something, as in His saying: ﴿When He wills a thing﴾ [Yasin: 82], ﴿He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ without delay and without need of any cause, as in His saying: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Qamar: 50], that is, Our command is only issued once, with no repetition, so that thing comes into being swiftly, like the blink of an eye. The discussion of this verse has already passed in Surat al-Baqarah.

(p-846)

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[48] ﴿And He will teach him the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel.﴾

﴿And He will teach him the Book⁠﴾ — i.e., writing, or the category of divine books. ﴿And wisdom⁠﴾ — i.e., refinement of character (tahdhib al-akhlaq). ﴿And the Torah and the Gospel⁠﴾ — singling them out by mention, on the assumption that by "the Book" is meant the category of revealed books, is for the sake of increasing their merit and their preeminence over others.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[49] ﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel, [saying]: "Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: that I create for you from clay the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission. And I heal the blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers."﴾

﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel﴾ is in the accusative case, governed by an implied verb that the meaning leads to, and it is coordinated with (yu'allimuhu) ("He will teach him"), meaning: "and He will make him a messenger to all the Israelites." It was also said that it is coordinated with the preceding circumstances (ahwal, sing. hal, "circumstantial clauses"): ﴿that I have come to you﴾ is the object of (rasulan) ("a messenger") because of the sense of speaking that it contains, meaning: a messenger speaking that "I have come to you": ﴿with a sign from your Lord﴾. The tanwin (nunation) on (ayah) ("sign") is for magnification, not for unity, since their multiplicity is evident. The prepositional phrase is attached to an omitted element that functions as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: "clothed in and offering as proof a sign": ﴿that I create for you from clay the form of a bird, then I breathe into it﴾. The pronoun (fihi, "in it") refers to the kaf (the "like" of the phrase "like the form of a bird"), meaning: into that thing resembling the form of a bird. ﴿and it becomes a bird﴾ real, possessing life. ﴿by Allah's permission﴾, meaning: by His command, not by any independent power of mine. ﴿And I heal the blind﴾, the one born blind. ﴿and the leper﴾, the one afflicted with leprosy (baras), which is a whiteness that appears on the skin due to imbalance of temperament. In al-Iklil (al-Iklil, a work cited on this verse), it is said: this verse is the basis for what physicians say: that the blind from birth (al-akmah, the one born blind) and the leper cannot be cured, just as the raising of the dead cannot be done. ﴿And I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission﴾, not by any independent power of mine, negating the suspicion of divinity (uluhiyyah) (p-847). These are compelling, practical miracles. ﴿And I inform you﴾, meaning: I tell you ﴿of what you eat and what you store in your houses﴾ of things I have not witnessed. ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾, meaning: a proof ﴿for you﴾ of my truthfulness in my claim to prophethood. ﴿if you are believers﴾, meaning: affirming the signs of Allah.

It is mentioned in the Gospel (al-Injil) that he, peace be upon him, restored the sight of two blind men in Kafr Nahum, and a blind man in Bayt Sayda, and a man born blind in Urshalim (Jerusalem); he healed ten lepers in Samaria, cured a leper in Kafr Nahum, raised the son of the widow from death in the town of Nayin, and brought back to life the daughter of Jairus in Kafr Nahum, and Lazarus in Bayt Ayna.

**Discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, the Exalted:**

[50] ﴿And confirming what was before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord. So fear Allah and obey me.﴾

﴿And confirming﴾ is a circumstantial phrase (حالٌ, ḥāl) conjoined to his words "بِآيَةٍ" (with a sign). That is: "I have come to you with a sign, and confirming..." ﴿what was before me of the Torah﴾ means: affirming it and establishing it. ﴿And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾. Ibn Kathir said: "In this there is evidence that ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) abrogated (نَسَخَ, naskh) some of the Torah's law, and this is the correct of the two opinions. Among the scholars is one who said: he abrogated nothing from it, but rather he made lawful for them some of what they had been disputing over in error, and the truth of that was revealed to them, as He said in the other verse: ﴿and to clarify for you some of that over which you differ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 63]. And Allah knows best." End of quote.

I say: Among the "some" that ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) made lawful for them was doing good on the Sabbath. They had believed in the prohibition of every kind of work on the Sabbath day. For this reason, when he (peace be upon him) passed by the Israelites once, he saw a sick man, and they asked him: "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?" He (peace be upon him) said to them: "Which one of you, if he has a sheep that falls into a pit on the Sabbath day (p-848) and does not take hold of it and lift it out? And how much better is a man than a sheep? So doing good is lawful on the Sabbath." Then he healed that sick man. Thus it is in chapter 12, verses 9 to 13, of the Gospel of Matthew. And in it, in chapter 5, verse 17, is the saying of the Messiah (peace be upon him): "Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I did not come to abolish but to fulfil." End of quote.

They have agreed that the Messiah (peace be upon him) upheld all the laws of the Torah. Then Paul (Bulus) and those after him among the monks came and claimed that the Messiah (peace be upon him) did all of that and lifted it from them, since he perfected and completed it by his own act. He spared them the burden of acting on any part of it and enriched them with his "spiritual" law. So they abolished the Law (al-Nāmūs) which the Messiah had come to complete. Among what they abolished was the permission of many animals that were forbidden in the Mosaic Law, so their prohibition was abrogated in the Christian law, and general permission was established by the ruling of Paul, when he said to them: "Nothing is unclean in itself," as in his epistle to the people of Rome. Among what they abolished was the glorification of the Sabbath. It had been an everlasting ruling in the Mosaic law, and no one was allowed to perform the least work on it, and whoever did work on it was deserving of death. Among it are the rulings on the festivals prescribed in the Torah. Among it is the ruling on circumcision, which had been everlasting in the law of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his descendants down to the law of Musa. ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) was circumcised, but the monks after him abrogated its ruling, just as they abrogated all the practical rulings of the Torah except fornication. This is explained in *Izhar al-Haqq* (Revealing the Truth), in the third chapter on proving abrogation. We have already set forth an important discussion on this matter in Surah al-Baqarah at His words: ﴿They say: "Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 135], so refer to it there.

﴿And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord﴾: he repeated it for emphasis, so that His words ﴿So fear Allah and obey me﴾ may be built upon it.

(p-849)

The discussion of His statement, may He be exalted:

[51] ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this﴾ means: what I command you with, ﴿is a straight path﴾.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[52] ﴿So when Jesus perceived disbelief from them, he said, "Who are my helpers in (the cause of) God?" The disciples (al-hawariyyun) said, "We are the helpers of God. We have believed in God, so bear witness that we are Muslims."﴾

﴿When Jesus perceived from them﴾ i.e., from the Children of Israel, ﴿disbelief﴾ i.e., he knew it and found it in them. ﴿He said, "Who are my helpers in (the cause of) God?"﴾ ''Ansar'' is the plural of ''nasir'' (helper). The prepositional phrase ''ila Allah'' is related to an omitted element that stands as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: "Who are my helpers, turning toward God and seeking refuge in Him?" ﴿The disciples (al-hawariyyun) said﴾ They are a group from the Children of Israel who were singled out for belief in the Messiah, peace be upon him; they supported him, aided him, and followed the light that was sent down with him. ''Hawariyyun'' is the plural of ''hawari'' (disciple), who is the helper, or one who is exaggerated in giving support; it also means a minister, an intimate friend, and a pure one, as in (al-Tawshih).[Note: this gloss is from the source text.] ﴿We are the helpers of God﴾ i.e., the helpers of His religion and His messenger. ﴿We have believed in God, so bear witness that we are Muslims﴾ i.e., submitting to your mission. When they had called upon him, peace be upon him, to bear witness, they called upon God, exalted is He, who commands what was sent down of belief in Him and His commands, and so they said:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 53:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[53] ﴿Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down and have followed the Messenger, so inscribe us among the witnesses.﴾

﴿Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down and have followed the Messenger﴾ — that is, we have called You to witness regarding what we are upon of our affirmation of it, as a claim. ﴿So inscribe us﴾ — that is, as a reward for our calling You to witness. ﴿Among the witnesses﴾ — that is, among those who bear witness to Your oneness. They are the ones mentioned in the verse ﴿Allah bears witness﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 18], or [it means] among the prophets who bear witness for their followers.

(p-850) A subtle point:

The Gospel of Matthew, in the tenth chapter, contains the following:

1 - Then he called his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, so that they might cast them out and heal every disease and every infirmity.

2 - Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother.

3 - Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus called Thaddaeus.

4 - Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.

They were called the messengers (rusul) of Jesus, peace be upon him, because he sent them to the misguided Children of Israel, calling them to the truth he had brought. They exerted effort in spreading it, disseminating it, and establishing it, until Paul came and, by his deception, stripped them of the true religion of the Messiah. They never heard any news from him afterward, nor did they find any trace of him. He obliterated for them the ordinances of the Torah and made lawful for them every forbidden thing, as has been explained in other places.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[54] ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers.﴾

﴿And they schemed﴾: that is, those whom Jesus, peace be upon him, perceived to be disbelieving, in that they resolved to kill him and intended him harm, when they conspired against him and reported him to their king.

﴿And Allah schemed﴾: that is, against them after that, so He took vengeance upon them, left them in lasting humiliation, and annihilated their kingdom.

﴿And Allah is the best of schemers﴾: that is, the most powerful of them in scheming, the most effective of them in plotting, and the most capable of inflicting harm from where they do not reckon.

Al-Biqa'i, like others, said regarding His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And Allah schemed﴾: that is, by raising him to Himself, and He made the matter appear to them, so that they thought they had crucified him, whereas they had only crucified one of them, and it is said that he was the one who pointed them to him. As for him, peace be upon him, Allah preserved him in His presence after raising him (p-851) to the abode of His friends and the place of His holiness, so that He would send him down at the end of time to annihilate them, after humiliation had been decreed upon them, following their intent to harm him by which they sought glory, until the end of time. Thus their destruction was in their own scheming.

Then Allah, exalted is He, announced the good tidings of his protection from their scheming by His saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 55:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[55] ﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, I will take you in and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve, and I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ."﴾

﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, I will take you in"﴾ That is, "I will complete the term of your stay among your people." The word tawaffi, as it is used for causing death, is likewise used for completing something, as is found in the books of lexicography. And if it is claimed that tawaffi is literally (haqiqah) in the first sense, and the basic principle in usage is the literal sense, we say: there is no barrier to likening the cessation of his peace be upon him authority over his followers, and the ending of his appointed term among them, to the removal of life. This interpretation is very clear, and it has parallels in the Noble Book. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep﴾ [al-Zumar: 42]. Al-Zamakhshari said: He means: "and He takes the souls that have not died in their sleep," that is, He takes them when they sleep, likening sleepers to the dead, and from this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who takes you in the night﴾ [al-An'am: 60], where they do not discern nor act, just as the dead are likewise. End of his words. Then, in His glad tidings of elevation to the place of His honour, the abode of His angels, and the source of purity from defilements, He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve﴾, that is, from their deception and the evil of their companionship. This verse, by its apparent meaning, indicates that Allah, exalted is He, is above His heavens, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Rather, Allah raised him to Himself; and Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾ [al-Nisa': 158], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Nahl: 50], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him﴾ [al-Sajdah: 5], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you secure from He who is in the heaven that He will cause the earth to swallow you, and then it will quake?﴾ [al-Mulk: 16]. This is the doctrine of the Salaf entirely, as Imam al-Dhahabi transmitted it in the book (al-'Uluww).

Abu al-Walid Ibn Rushd said in (Manahij al-Adillah): The people of the Shari'ah have, from the very beginning, affirmed for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, the direction of (above), until the Mu'tazilah denied it, and after them the later Ash'ariyyah followed them in denying it, such as Abu al-Ma'ali and those who followed his statement. He went on to say: All the revealed laws are founded upon the fact that Allah is in the heaven, that from Him the angels descend with revelation to the prophets, that the books were sent down from the heavens, and that the Night Journey of the Prophet ﷺ was towards them. All the philosophers have agreed that Allah and the angels are in the heaven, just as all the revealed laws have agreed upon that by reason. He clarified the falsehood of the doubt for which the Jahmiyyah and those who agreed with them denied it. He went on to say: It has become clear to you from this that affirming the direction is obligatory by revelation and reason, and that negating it is the negation of the revealed laws. Al-Darimi said: The Muslims have unanimously agreed that Allah is above His Throne, above His heavens. Al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi has expounded the texts of the Salaf in the book (al-'Uluww), so refer to it.

(p-853) Since people of lofty aspirations pay the closest attention to what their successors will be like after them in circumstances, He, exalted is He, gave him glad tidings in that regard with what He gave him glad tidings of, saying: ﴿and I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾. Thus it has always been that those who adopt Christianity have been above the Jews, and they will remain so until they are annihilated, such that none of them remains: ﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ.﴾ Then He explained the judgment that takes place between the two groups with His saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieved, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 56].

The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wil*) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[56] ﴿As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.﴾

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[57] ﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers.﴾ That is: He hates them. This figurative usage (kinayah) is widespread in all languages, functioning in the manner of a literal expression.

**The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

[58] ﴿That, We recite it to you, of the signs and the Wise Reminder.﴾

﴿That﴾ refers to what preceded of the account of ʿIsa (Jesus), peace be upon him. It is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate (khabar) is: ﴿We recite it to you﴾, meaning without you having had any prior knowledge of it. His words, Exalted is He: ﴿of the signs﴾ are a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the object pronoun, or a second predicate after the first: ﴿and the Wise Reminder﴾, meaning the one containing wisdoms, or the one that is firm (muhkam), protected from any defect reaching it. What is meant by it is the Qur'an.

**Note:**

Regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, I will take you in death﴾ [Al ʿImran: 55], there are many interpretations. However, the one the Master (al-Mawla) opened up through what we have previously stated is the most preponderant of the interpretations, and God knows best. By it, the claim of the Christians falls away, that this verse is an argument against us, since it indicates that he died, i.e., by crucifixion, then his being raised to the heavens, meaning his standing alive after his death according to their claim, that he died in his body and remained on the cross until the time of sunset on Friday, then was taken down and buried at the first hour of the night of Saturday, remained in the tomb until the morning of Sunday, then rose alive, and appeared to the women who had come to his tomb as visitors. They based this claim on the testimony of their four Gospels, and on the oral testimony of his disciples throughout the world, then their followers, and likewise on the testimony of the Jews that the crucifixion did occur upon the Messiah in person. The way their aforementioned corrupt claim falls is what we have explained concerning the meaning of the verse, which leaves no slightest doubt. Our scholars have clarified the falsity of this belief of theirs in various compositions and treatises, so refer to (the margins of Tuhfat al-Arib fi al-Radd ʿala Ahl al-Salib) by the Shaykh ʿAbd Allah Bik.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[59] ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus in the sight of Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾

﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus﴾ means: his wondrous state in being brought into existence by power, without a father. ﴿In the sight of Allah﴾ means: in His decree and judgment. ﴿Like the likeness of Adam﴾ means: like his wondrous condition, about which no doubter has doubt. ﴿He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ is a clause explaining the comparison by clarifying the point of resemblance between them, and a cutting off of the basis of the opponents' doubts. For denying the creation of Jesus, peace be upon him, without a father, from one who has acknowledged the creation of Adam, peace be upon him, without a father or mother, is something that hardly holds up. So said Abu al-Su'ud. His words ﴿He created him﴾ mean: He shaped the body of Adam from dust; ﴿then He said to him, "Be"﴾ means: a complete human being, spirit and body. For His command, exalted is He, conveys the power of bringing into being. Al-Biqa'i said: He expressed it with the present tense conjoined with the fa' in ﴿and he was﴾ rather than the past tense, although what comes first to mind is that the meaning is for narrating the situation and depicting it; this indicates that the matter occurred without any failure, and it draws attention to the fact that this is always the case, renewing itself with every intended thing, never failing to match the will of the Commander at all, as was previously stated explicitly in the verse ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾ [Al 'Imran: 47].

A subtle point:

Al-Razi said: The wise have said that Adam, peace be upon him, was created from dust for several reasons:

The first: so that he would be humble.

The second: so that he would be a veil.

The third: so that he would cling more closely to the earth. This is because he was created to be the successor of the people of the earth. The Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30].

The fourth: the Truth wished to manifest power, so He created the devils from fire, which is the brightest of bodies, and tested them with the darknesses of misguidance; and He created Adam from dust, which is the densest of bodies, then gave him love, knowledge, light and guidance.

The fifth: He created man from dust so that he would extinguish the fire of desire and anger. End of the summary.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[60] ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾

﴿The truth is from your Lord﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: the account of Jesus that We have related to you is the truth. It has also been said: "al-Haqq" (the truth) is the subject and the prepositional phrase is the predicate, meaning: the truth mentioned. It has further been said: "al-Haqq" is the subject of an implied verb, meaning: the truth has come to you. Regarding "al-Haqq" there are two interpretations:

The first: Abu Muslim said: The intended meaning is that this which We have sent down to you (p-856) is the truth concerning the report of Jesus, peace be upon him, not what the Christians and the Jews say. The Christians say that Mary gave birth to a god, and the Jews accused Mary, peace be upon her, of slander and attributed her to Yusuf the carpenter. So Allah, Exalted is He, made clear that what He sent down in the Qur'an is the truth, and then forbade doubt concerning it.

The second view: the intended meaning is that the truth in explaining this matter is the parable we mentioned, namely the story of Adam, peace be upon him, for there is no clearer explanation than it. And Allah knows best.

﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾ is an address either to the Prophet ﷺ in the manner of stirring him up to increase his steadfastness, or to every listener.

The discussion of His words, Exalted is He:

[61] ﴿Then whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you, say: "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us earnestly invoke Allah and lay the curse of Allah upon the liars."﴾

﴿Whoever argues with you﴾: that is, disputes with you from among the Christians by presenting an argument, ﴿concerning it﴾: that is, concerning the matter of ʿIsa (Jesus), claiming that he is not in the state described in the recitation, ﴿after the knowledge has come to you﴾: that is, what We sent down to you and related to you concerning his affair. Al-Fadil al-Mahayimi has a subtle method of interpretation regarding this verse, where he said: ﴿The truth﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 60], that is, the established reality that does not accept interpretation, has come ﴿from your Lord﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 60], who nurtured you through acquainting you with the realities, ﴿so do not be of those who doubt﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 60] regarding what occurs in the Gospel of applying the word "Father" to Allah, for that is a metaphorical application, since He, when He originated him, was like his father. And when the truth has become manifest to you from your Lord through complete clarification, ﴿whoever argues with you﴾: that is, disputes with you ﴿concerning it﴾ in order to establish his sonship by the apparent meanings of the Gospel, ﴿after the knowledge has come to you﴾, the definitive knowledge that necessitates its interpretation. ﴿Then say﴾: there remains no debate between us and you, but We will remove your obstinacy by way of mubahala (mutual invocation of a curse, a form of ordeal-prayer): ﴿Come﴾: that is, approach, you disputants, toward a matter in which the exaltedness of the truth and the lowliness of falsehood are recognized: ﴿let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves﴾: that is, each of us and you calls upon his own self, his dear family members, and those closest to his heart, for whose sake a man risks himself, fights in their defense, and brings them along to the mubahala. ﴿Then let us earnestly invoke﴾: that is, let us humble ourselves before Allah, Exalted, and strive in supplicating for the curse ﴿so that We lay the curse of Allah﴾: that is, His removal and expulsion ﴿upon the liars﴾ among us and among you, so that Allah destroys them and saves the truthful. Thus the remaining obstinacy upon you will not persist after the agreement of the rational and transmitted proofs.

Notes:

First: Al-Qashani said: The mubahala of the prophets has a great effect, its cause being the connection of their souls to the Holy Spirit and Allah's support of them through it. It is the one that acts, by Allah's permission, upon the elemental world. Thus the elemental world is affected by it as our body is affected by our spirit through the states that come upon it, such as anger, grief, and thought concerning the state of the beloved, and other movements of the limbs at the arising of wills and resolutions. The human souls are affected by it as our senses and all our faculties are affected by the states of our spirits. So when a holy soul connects with it, its influence on the world, at the directed moment of connection, is by the influence of what it connects with, and thus the bodies of the elements and the imperfect human souls are affected by what it wills. Have you not seen how the souls of the Christians were affected by fear from his soul, peace be upon him, and refrained from mubahala, and sought reconciliation by accepting the jizya (poll tax)?!

Second: Ibn Kathir said: The occasion of revelation of this mubahala and what precedes it from the beginning of the sura up to here was the delegation of the Christians of Najran when they came to Madina. They began to dispute concerning ʿIsa and claimed about him what they claimed of sonship and divinity. So Allah revealed the opening of this sura in refutation of them, as mentioned by Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others. They were sixty riders, among them three men to whom their affairs returned: al-ʿAqib, the leader of the people, whose name was ʿAbd al-Masih; al-Sayyid, their chief in planning, and the companion of their caravan, whose name was al-Ayham; and Abu Haritha ibn ʿAlqama, their bishop and scholar. In the account: "When the news came to the Prophet (ﷺ) from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the decisive judgment between him and them, and he was commanded with what he was commanded regarding cursing them if they rejected that, he invited them to mubahala. They said: 'O Abu al-Qasim, leave us to consider our affair, then we will come to you with what we want to do regarding what you have invited us to.' So they departed from him. Then they withdrew with al-ʿAqib and said: 'O ʿAbd al-Masih, what do you think?' He said: 'By Allah, O company of Christians, you know that Muhammad is truly a sent prophet, and he has brought you the decisive account concerning your companion. You know that no people ever cursed a prophet, so their elder would not remain and their young would not grow. If you do it, it will surely be total destruction for you. So if you have refused except to cling to your religion and to remain in what you hold concerning your companion, then make peace with the man and return to your lands.' They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Abu al-Qasim! We have decided not to curse you, and to leave you upon your religion and return to our religion.' So he (ﷺ) did not curse them, and he confirmed them upon a tribute they would pay to him."

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated from al-Shaʿbi, from Jabir, who said: "Al-ʿAqib and al-Tayyib came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he invited them to mulaʿana (mutual cursing). They promised him that they would curse him the next morning. Jabir said: The Messenger of Allah went out in the morning, took ʿAli, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn by the hand, then sent for them, but they refused to respond and acknowledged the tribute to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'By Him who sent me with the truth, if they had said no, He would have rained fire upon them from the valley.'" Jabir said: It is concerning them that the verse ﴿Our sons﴾ was revealed. Jabir said: "Ourselves and yourselves" are the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ʿAli ibn Abi Talib; "our sons" are al-Hasan and al-Husayn; "our women" is Fatima. Thus al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak with this meaning, and then said: "It is sound according to the condition of Muslim, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Thus he said.

But Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it from Shuʿba, from al-Mughira, from al-Shaʿbi, as a mursal report (one in which the Successor reports directly from the Prophet, omitting the Companion), and this is more authentic.

Something similar has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Bara'.

Al-Bukhari narrated from Hudhayfa (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Al-ʿAqib and al-Sayyid, the two companions of Najran, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intending to curse him. One of them said to his companion: 'Do not do it, for by Allah, if he is a prophet and we curse him, neither we nor our descendants after us will prosper.' They said: 'We will give you what you ask of us, but send with us a trustworthy man, and send with us only a trustworthy man.' He said: 'I will surely send with you a man who is truly trustworthy.' The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then aspired to it. He said: 'Stand up, O Abu ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrah.' When he stood, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'This is the trustworthy one of this Ummah.'" Muslim, al-Nasa'i and others also narrated it.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Abu Jahl (may Allah curse him) said: "If I see Muhammad praying at the Kaʿba, I will surely come to him and step on his neck." He said: "If he were to do so, the angels would seize him before our eyes. And if the Jews wished for death, they would die, and they would see their places in the Fire. And if those who would perform mubahala with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had come out, they would have returned finding neither wealth nor family."

Ibn Kathir said: Al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i have narrated it. Imam Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) related the account of the Najran delegation in Zad al-Ma'ad and followed it with an important section on its jurisprudence, so let it be consulted.

Third: Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say: His invitation to mubahala was only so that the liar between him and his opponent would become evident, and that matter is specific to him and to the one who lies against him. What then is the meaning of including the sons and women? I say: That is more emphatic in indicating his confidence in his own state and his certainty of his truthfulness, since he boldly exposed his dearest ones, the fruits of his heart, and the people most beloved to him for this. He did not limit himself to exposing only his own self, and his knowledge of his confidence in the falsehood of his opponent, to the extent that his opponent would be destroyed together with his beloved ones and his dear ones with total annihilation, if the mubahala were completed. He specified the sons and women because they are the dearest of family and closest to the hearts; a man may ransom them with himself and fight in their defense until he is killed. For this reason they used to drive the women-folk with themselves in wars, so that they would prevent them from fleeing, and they called those who defend them with their lives "protectors of honor." He mentioned them before the selves in order to draw attention to their special place and nearness of rank, and to indicate that they are given precedence over the selves and are ransomed by them. In this there is evidence, with nothing stronger than it, of the excellence of the People of the Cloak, peace be upon them. In it is also clear proof of the soundness of the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ), because no one, of either supporter or opponent, has narrated that they accepted this.

Fourth: From the verse is derived the permissibility of argumentation in matters of religion, and that whoever disputes and denies something of the Shariʿa, his mubahala is permissible, following what the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to do. Mubahala means mulaʿana (mutual cursing).

Al-Kazaruni said in his tafsir: The question arose with our teacher, the scholar al-Dawani, may Allah sanctify his secret, regarding the permissibility of mubahala after the Prophet (ﷺ), and he wrote a treatise on its conditions derived from the Book, the Sunna, the reports, and the statements of the imams. The essence of his words on it is: It is not permissible except in a matter of great importance in the Shariʿa, in which confusion and obstinacy have arisen that cannot be overcome except through mubahala. It is required that it be after the establishment of proof, striving to remove doubt, offering counsel and warning, and the failure of these to benefit, and the necessity to resort to it.

Imam Siddiq Khan said in his tafsir: The Hafiz Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, invited whoever opposed him on the question of the attributes of the Lord, may His affair be exalted, and their application according to their apparent meanings without interpretation, distortion, or negation, to mubahala between the Corner (of the Kaʿba) and the Station (of Ibrahim), but he (the opponent) did not respond to him and feared the evil consequence. The full account of this is mentioned at the beginning of his well-known book called al-Nuniyya. End of quotation. He mentioned in Zad al-Ma'ad, in the section on the jurisprudence of the account of the Najran delegation, the following text: Among its lessons is that the Sunna in disputing with the people of falsehood, when Allah's proof has been established against them and they do not return, but persist in obstinacy, is to invite them to mubahala. Allah, Glorified is He, commanded this to His Messenger, and did not say that this is not for your Ummah after you. Ibn ʿAmm him ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas invited to it whoever denied some of the subsidiary questions against him, and the Companions did not object to him. Al-Awza'i invited Sufyan al-Thawri to it in the question of raising the hands (in prayer), and that was not denied against him. This is part of the completeness of the proof. End of quotation.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[62] ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative. And there is no deity except Allah. And indeed, Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾

﴿Indeed, this﴾ — that is, what has preceded concerning the affair of ʿĪsā, peace be upon him — ﴿is the true narrative﴾, which admits of no deviation from it, unlike the fables of the Christians. Qiṣaṣ (narratives) follow the events by reporting them one after another in their proper order, in the sense of qaṣṣ al-athar (tracing a trail), which is following it until one arrives at the place of the one who left the trail. So said al-Ḥarrālī.

Al-Biqāʿī said: When He, glorified is He, began the narrative at the beginning of the surah by informing of His oneness, explicitly proving it by His being the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, He concluded that by way of allusion and hint. He said, linking it to what the preceding material produced — that ʿĪsā is the servant of Allah and His messenger — generalizing the ruling: ﴿And there is no deity except Allah﴾, expressing it with ﴿min﴾ (any) of comprehensive negation, as an emphatic refutation of the Christians in their trinitarianism. ﴿And indeed, Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾, so that no one shares with Him in might or wisdom, and thus no one shares with Him in divinity.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[63] ﴿And if they turn away, then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters.﴾

﴿And if they turn away﴾ means: they turn away from accepting the truth that was related to them after they had witnessed those clear proofs. ﴿Then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters﴾ means: Knowing of them, so He will recompense them for their corruption. The expression of them by this term indicates that they, by their turning away, are corrupters of their own belief and of the belief of others concerning Allah, exalted is He.

The discussion concerning the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, the Exalted:

[64] ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will worship none but Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah. And if they turn away, then say, 'Bear witness that we are Muslims.'"﴾

﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you"﴾ That is: to a statement that is moderate, which does not incline toward ta'til (denial of the divine attributes) nor toward shirk (association of partners with Allah), agreed upon, on which the messengers and the scriptures do not differ. And it is: ﴿that we will worship none but Allah and not associate anything with Him﴾, meaning: we do not regard anyone other than Him as deserving of worship so that we associate him with Him, but rather we single out worship for Allah alone, with no partner. This is the call of all the messengers. Allah, the Exalted, said: (p-862) ﴿We did not send any messenger before you except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 25]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We had certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"﴾ [An-Nahl: 36].

﴿and not take one another as lords﴾ That is: like Uzayr, al-Masih, the rabbis and the monks, who used to declare lawful for them and make unlawful for them. As al-Tirmidhi narrated from Adi ibn Hatim, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords instead of Allah﴾ [At-Tawbah: 31]. He said: 'They did not worship them, but when they declared something lawful for them, they considered it lawful, and when they declared something unlawful for them, they considered it unlawful.'"

Al-Kiya al-Harrasi said: In this there is a refutation of those who say [legal ruling] by mere istihsan (juristic preference) that is not supported by a textual legal proof, and of those who say that it is obligatory to accept the word of the imam in declaring things lawful and unlawful even without showing a textual basis.

Al-Biqa'i said: Since the Lord (Rabb) may be applied to a teacher and a trainer in some kind of upbringing, He drew attention to the fact that what is to be feared is only the belief in independent authority and presumption regarding what is exclusively Allah's. So He said: ﴿instead of Allah﴾, who alone is characterized by perfection. ﴿And if they turn away﴾, that is, from this equitable word upon which there is agreement. ﴿Then say﴾, that is, following your father Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when he said: "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds" [Al-Baqarah: 131], and in compliance with his charge when he said: ﴿And do not die except as Muslims﴾ [Al-i-Imran: 102]. ﴿Bear witness that we are Muslims﴾, that is: the proof has been established against you, so it is obligatory upon you to acknowledge that we are Muslims, not you. This is like the victor saying to the vanquished in a dispute, a contest, or otherwise: "Acknowledge that I am the victor, and yield to me the victory." It may also be of the nature of allusion (ta'ridh), and its meaning would be: "Bear witness and acknowledge that you are disbelievers, since you have turned away from the truth after its manifestation." Thus said (al-Kashshaf). (p-863)

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[65] ﴿O People of the Book, why do you argue about Abraham, when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Will you not then use your reason?﴾

﴿O People of the Book, why do you argue about Abraham﴾, i.e., you dispute concerning him, each of your two groups claiming him for itself. ﴿When the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him﴾, i.e., each of them affirms the foundation of the religion of its adherents among you. ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾, so that you would not engage in this impossible kind of disputation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 66:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[66] ﴿Ha antum ha'ulaa' hajajtum fima lakum bihi 'ilm, falima tuhajjoona fima laysa lakum bihi 'ilm? Wallahu ya'lamu wa antum la ta'lamoon.﴾

﴿Ha antum ha'ulaa'﴾ means: you, these foolish persons. ﴿Hajajtum fima lakum bihi 'ilm﴾ concerns the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ), since he is mentioned in your Book, so it was possible for you to alter it in wording and meaning; or it concerns the matter of Musa and Isa, peace be upon them both, or what the Torah and the Gospel have spoken of. ﴿Falima tuhajjoona fima laysa lakum bihi 'ilm﴾ concerns the matter of Ibrahim, because he is not mentioned in your Book in the manner in which you argued, so you cannot alter it. ﴿Wallahu ya'lamu﴾ so He makes it clear to His Prophet. ﴿Wa antum la ta'lamoon﴾

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[67] ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a true monotheist (ḥanīf), a Muslim, and he was not one of the polytheists.﴾

﴿Abraham was not a Jew﴾, i.e., as the Jews claimed. ﴿Nor a Christian﴾, as the Christians claimed. ﴿But he was a true monotheist (ḥanīf), a Muslim﴾. The meaning of ḥanīf (one who turns away from falsehood toward pure monotheism) has already been explained at His words, the Exalted: ﴿Rather, [follow] the religion of Abraham, a ḥanīf﴾ [al-Baqarah: 135], in Surat al-Baqarah. ﴿And he was not one of the polytheists﴾ is an implicit reproach to them, since they are polytheists by their saying: "Uzayr is the son of God" and "the Messiah is the son of God," and it is a refutation of the claim of the polytheists that they are upon the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him.

(p-864)

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 68:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[68] ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believed; and Allah is the Ally of the believers.﴾

﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham﴾ means: those most specially connected to him and nearest to him, from al-wali (al-wilaya, "nearness"). ﴿Are those who followed him﴾ means: in his religion, from among his community and others. ﴿And this Prophet﴾ means: the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And those who believed﴾ means: in him, and who acted according to his Sharia, which agrees with the Sharia of Abraham. ﴿And Allah is the Ally of the believers﴾ means: by granting victory, aid, and love.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[69] ﴿A group of the People of the Book wish they could lead you astray, but they lead astray none except themselves, and they do not perceive.﴾

﴿Wished﴾, i.e., desired: ﴿a group of the People of the Book wish they could lead you astray﴾ by returning you to their religion, out of envy and spite. ﴿But they lead astray none except themselves﴾, i.e., the misguidance does not pass beyond them, and its burden returns only upon them, since their punishment is multiplied because of it. ﴿And they do not perceive﴾, i.e., that its burden is specifically theirs. A parallel to this verse is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into disbelievers after your faith, out of envy from themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 109], and His saying: ﴿They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved, so that you would be equal﴾ [al-Nisa': 89].

(p-865)

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[70] ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of God while you witness [their truth]?﴾

﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of God﴾ i.e., those revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿While you witness﴾ i.e., you know their reality.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[71] ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you mix the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know [it]?﴾

﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you mix the truth with falsehood?﴾ That is: you cover up the truth that was revealed with your false embellishments. ﴿And conceal the truth﴾ That is: the truth that does not accept embellishment or distortion. ﴿While you know﴾ That is: knowing what you conceal of its truthfulness. They indeed knew what is in the Torah and the Gospel of the good tidings of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his prophethood, and they used to confuse the people about that, just as was their custom regarding other matters. In the verse there is an indication of the ugliness of concealing the truth, and this includes the foundations of the religion and its branches, legal rulings (fatwa) and testimony. And [it indicates] the ugliness of deception (talbis). Therefore it is obligatory to resolve doubt (shubha) and nullify it.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 72:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[72] ﴿And a faction of the People of the Book said: "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they may return."﴾

﴿And a faction of the People of the Book said: "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day"﴾ i.e., its first part; ﴿and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they may return﴾. This verse recounts another kind of their deceptions (p-866). It is a scheme they intended in order to confuse the weak among the believers regarding the matter of their religion. Their plan was that they consulted among themselves to show faith at the beginning of the day and pray with the Muslims, and then when the end of the day came, they would apostatize back to their religion. The weak would thus think that they have no aim but the truth, and that nothing turned them away from the religion after following it and abandoning obstinacy, and they are people of knowledge and of the Book, except that its falsehood became evident to them. For this reason He said: ﴿that perhaps they may return﴾, i.e., from Islam, just as you returned.

A subtle point:

Al-Razi said: The benefit in God Most High informing about their collusion over this stratagem is in several respects:

The first: that this stratagem was hidden among them, and they did not disclose it to anyone outside of them. So when the Messenger informed about it, that was an announcement of the unseen, and thus it is a miracle.

The second: that when God Most High informed the believers of their collusion over this stratagem, it had no effect on the hearts of the believers; and had this notification not occurred, it might well have affected the heart of someone whose faith was weak.

The third: that when these people were exposed in this stratagem, that became a deterrent preventing them from undertaking similar tricks and deceptions.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[73] ﴿And do not believe except for one who follows your religion. Say, "Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of Allah, [and] that someone be given the like of what you were given, or that they should argue with you before your Lord." Say, "Indeed, bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing."﴾

﴿And do not believe except for one who follows your religion﴾ is part of their speech, meaning: do not affirm [the truth] except for a prophet who follows your law, not one who comes with other than it. Or it means: do not believe that earlier belief, which was their belief at the start of the day, except for the sake of preserving your followers and adherents and keeping them upon your religion. ﴿Say, "Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of Allah"﴾, meaning: that which is Islam, and I have brought it to you, and anything other than it is misguidance. So this feeble scheme will not benefit you in repelling it, and you cannot lead astray any one of us after Allah has guided us. Then He connected to it their rebuke, saying: ﴿أنْ﴾ with the alif prolonged as an interrogative, according to the reading of Ibn Kathir. In the reading of others, it is taken as an implied "that" (an), meaning: envy and insolence prompted you until you said what you said and plotted it now: ﴿that someone be given the like of what you were given﴾, of the laws, knowledge and Book; ﴿or﴾ out of dislike that ﴿they should argue with you﴾, meaning: those who were given the like of what you were given; ﴿before your Lord﴾, meaning: by testifying against you on the Day of Resurrection that they believed and you disbelieved after the clear explanation, so that it would expose you. ﴿Say, "Indeed, the bounty"﴾, meaning: by sending down the signs and other things, ﴿is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾, so you cannot prevent it. ﴿And Allah is all-Encompassing﴾, abundant in giving; ﴿Knowing﴾.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[74] ﴿He singles out for His mercy whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾

﴿He singles out for His mercy whom He wills﴾ — so He grants him more bounty than you: ﴿and God is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 75:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[75] ﴿And among the People of the Scripture is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you unless you constantly stand over him. That is because they say, "There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered." And they speak falsely about Allah while they know it.﴾

﴿And among the People of the Scripture is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you unless you constantly stand over him﴾ — by way of demanding (it back), litigating, and establishing proof. So it is not far-fetched that he would commit treachery against Allah by concealing what He commanded him to make manifest, out of greed for preserving leadership and the bribe he receives. Then he resumed (speaking about) the cause of the treachery with His saying: ﴿That is because they say, "There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered"﴾. That is: this permitting of themselves and this treachery is due to the fact that they say: there is no punishment or accountability for us regarding what we have taken from the wealth of the Arabs. (p-868) Thus they betray the creation. ﴿And they speak﴾, that is, in justifying this: ﴿falsely about Allah﴾ by their claim of that and other things, so they also betray Him. ﴿While they know﴾ that it is pure falsehood and fabrication, since treachery is forbidden to them, as it is in the Torah. Its transmission has already passed in al-Baqarah, at the verse: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews﴾ [al-Baqarah: 62], so refer back to it.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 76:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[76] ﴿Yes! Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of God—indeed, God loves the mindful.﴾

﴿Yes!
