Imam Ahmad narrated from Jariyah ibn Qudamah al-Sa'di that he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me a saying that will benefit me, and keep it brief for me, that I may retain it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not become angry." He repeated it to him, until he had repeated it to him several times, each time saying: "Do not become angry." (Ahmad alone narrated it.) It was also narrated by another route that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He said: "Do not become angry." The man said: "I reflected when the Prophet (ﷺ) said what he said, and I found that anger gathers all evil." ﴿And those who pardon people﴾, i.e., their wrongdoing against them, even if they have killed some of them, so they do not hold anyone accountable for what he commits against them, and no resentment remains in their souls, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when they are angry, they forgive﴾ [al-Shura: 37]. Imam al-Qaffal, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is possible that this refers back to what was censured of the polytheists' practice of usury, so the believers were forbidden from that and were encouraged to pardon the debtors in difficulty. Allah, exalted is He, said after the account of usury and debt: ﴿And if someone is in hardship, then let there be postponement until a time of ease. And that you give charity is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [al-Baqarah: 280]. It is also possible that it is as He, exalted is He, said regarding blood money: ﴿But if he is pardoned by his brother in anything﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178], up to His saying: ﴿And that you give charity is better for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 280]. It is also possible (p-975) that this was occasioned by the anger of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they mutilated Hamzah, and he said: "I will surely mutilate them." So he was encouraged to suppress this anger and to be patient with it, and to refrain from doing what he had said he would do of mutilation; thus his abstention from doing that was a pardon. Allah, exalted is He, said concerning this incident: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient﴾ [al-Nahl: 126]. End of quotation.

It is evident that the generality of the verse includes all that has been mentioned, since there is no specification. ﴿And Allah loves the doers of good.﴾ The lam may be for the category (genus), and they are included in it primarily. Or it may be for a specific reference, and He described them as "the doers of good," signifying that the attributes enumerated fall under ihsan, which is performing deeds in the proper manner, the descriptive goodness of which necessitates their intrinsic goodness. The Prophet (ﷺ) explained it by saying: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you." The sentence is a concluding statement (tadhyil) confirming the content of what precedes it, as Abu al-Su'ud stated.

(p-976)

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 135:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[135] ﴿And those who, when they commit an immoral act or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins except Allah? — and do not persist in what they have done while they know.﴾

﴿And those who, when they commit an immoral act﴾ — from the major evil deeds. ﴿Or wrong themselves﴾ — meaning, by any kind of sin. ﴿Remember Allah﴾ — meaning, they recall His right and His covenant, so they feel shame before Him and fear Him. ﴿And seek forgiveness for their sins﴾ — meaning, for the sake of them, by repentance and turning back to Him, exalted is He.

Al-Biqa'i said: Since this implies that He forgives them, because He is Oft-Forgiving to those who repent, He followed it with the confirmation of this and the denial of the power to do so to anyone else, encouraging turning to Him, by inserting between the two conjoined elements His saying: ﴿And who forgives sins﴾ — meaning, erases their traces so that they are not mentioned, and they are not requited for them. ﴿Except Allah﴾ — meaning, the Supreme King.

Abu al-Su'ud said: "Man" (من) is an interrogative of denial, meaning: no one forgives sins except Allah. However, the indication of negation through the interrogative is stronger and more emphatic, since it signals that every person who has a share of address knows that negation, so he hastens to answer with it. The purpose is to describe Him, glorified is He, with the utmost breadth of mercy and the generality of forgiveness. The sentence is parenthetical between the two conjoined elements, or between the circumstantial clause and its referent, to affirm seeking forgiveness and urge it, and to convey the promise of acceptance.

Al-Zamakhshari said: In this sentence there is a description of His essence, exalted is He, with the breadth of mercy and the nearness of forgiveness, and that the one who repents of sin is in His sight as one who has no sin; that there is no refuge for the sinners except His bounty and generosity; and that His justice requires forgiveness for the penitent, because when the servant comes with his utmost capacity in apology and disavowal, pardon and overlooking become obligatory. In it there is consolation for the hearts of the servants, encouragement to repentance, incitement to it, and deterrence from despair and hopelessness; and that sins, however great, His pardon is greater, and His generosity is more magnificent. The meaning: He alone possesses the means that make forgiveness valid. — End.

(p-977) In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from al-Aswad ibn Sari' (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) was brought a captive, and he said: "O Allah, I repent to You and do not repent to Muhammad." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He recognized the truth for its people." And in it also, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Iblis said to his Lord: 'By Your might and Your majesty, I will not cease to mislead the children of Adam as long as the souls are in them.' Allah said: 'By My might and My majesty, I will not cease to forgive them as long as they seek forgiveness from Me.'"

And in it also, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "When I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah benefited me by what He willed from it, and when someone else related it to me, I made him swear. When he swore to me, I believed him. And Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) related to me, and Abu Bakr spoke truly, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'No man commits a sin and then performs ablution, perfecting the ablution, then prays two rak'ahs, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that He forgives him.'" It was related by the people of the Sunan, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and others. al-Tirmidhi said: It is a hasan hadith.

﴿And do not persist﴾ — meaning, they do not remain: ﴿in what they have done﴾ — meaning, the sins they committed, without seeking forgiveness. ﴿While they know﴾ — a circumstantial clause from the subject of "do not persist": meaning, they do not persist in what they have done while they are aware of its ugliness, of the prohibition against it, and of the threat upon it. The restriction by this is because one who does not know the ugliness of the ugly act may be excused.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Bazzar and Abu Ya'la related from a client (mawla) of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), from Abu Bakr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One who seeks forgiveness does not persist, even if he returns to it seventy times in a day." (p-978) Its chain is not objectionable. Ibn Kathir said: The statement of Ali ibn al-Madini and al-Tirmidhi, "The chain of this hadith is not strong," apparently is due to the unknown status of Abu Bakr's client; but the unknown status of such a man does not harm, since he is a senior Successor (tabi'i), and his attribution to Abu Bakr suffices for him; so it is a hasan hadith. And Allah knows best.

The statement concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[136] ﴿Those—their reward is forgiveness from their Lord, and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein; and excellent is the reward of the workers.﴾

﴿Those﴾ refers to those previously mentioned, in consideration of their being characterized by the praiseworthy attributes that preceded. ﴿Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord﴾, meaning a covering over of their sins. ﴿And gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning rivers of various kinds of drinks. ﴿Abiding therein; and excellent is the reward of the workers﴾. The al-makhsus bi'l-madh (the specified object of praise) is omitted, meaning: that, i.e., what was mentioned of forgiveness and gardens. Then the revelation returned to detailing the remainder of the story of Uhud, after its preface of the principles of guidance and righteousness with His words:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 137:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[137] ﴿Indeed, there have passed before you examples (sunan). So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those who denied.﴾

﴿Indeed, there have passed﴾ means: have gone by. ﴿before you examples (sunan)﴾ means: occurrences of various kinds of punishments and calamities befalling the nations who denied. ﴿So travel through the earth﴾ — the earth in which are their ruined dwellings and the traces of their destruction. ﴿and observe how was the end of those who denied﴾ means: and measure by them the end of those who follow them in destruction and annihilation. The command to travel and to look is because witnessing the traces of earlier peoples has an effect on reflection (i'tibar), and the awe it produces is stronger than the effect of hearing.(p-979)

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[138] ﴿This is a clear statement for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for the God-fearing.﴾

﴿This⁠﴾ refers to the Qur'an, or to what has preceded of the chastisement of those mentioned: ﴿a clear statement for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition﴾, that is, a beneficial warning: ﴿for the God-fearing (al-muttaqin)⁠﴾. Then He strengthened the hearts of the believers and consoled them for what had befallen them with His saying:

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[139] ﴿So do not weaken, nor grieve, and you will have the upper hand if you are believers﴾

﴿So do not weaken, nor grieve, and you will have the upper hand if you are believers﴾ That is: do not become weak in jihad because of the wounds that have reached you, and do not grieve over those among you who were killed, while you are the superior ones, the victorious ones over your enemy, for the final outcome of their affair is destruction, as you have witnessed from the fate of their predecessors. This is an explicit promise of victory after an indication of it in what preceded. His saying, ﴿if you are believers﴾, is connected either to the prohibition or to "the superior ones" (al-a'lawna). Its response (jawab) is omitted, because what it is connected to indicates it. That is: if you are believers, then do not weaken and do not grieve, for faith requires strength of heart, reliance on the handiwork of God Exalted, and indifference to His enemies. Or: if you are believers, then you are the superior ones, for faith necessarily entails superiority. This was related by Abu al-Su'ud.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[140] ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people. And We alternate these days among the people, that Allah may know those who believe and take from among you martyrs. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿If a wound touches you﴾ — with the fatha and the damma are two readings, and they are two dialects, like ḍaʿf and ḍuʿf. That is: (p-980) if a wound has afflicted you on the Day of Uhud. ﴿Then a similar wound has touched the people﴾, that is, on the Day of Badr. They did not weaken and did not lose heart, so you are more deserving [of steadfastness], because you are promised victory over them. That is: you are equal in the pain, but you differ in hope and reward, as He said: ﴿If you suffer, indeed they suffer as you suffer, but you hope from Allah for what they do not hope﴾ [al-Nisa: 104]. So why do you falter and weaken at the wound and the pain, when that befell them in the way of Satan, while you were struck in the way of Allah and seeking His pleasure? It was also said: both touches were on the Day of Uhud, for the Muslims inflicted losses on them before they disobeyed the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿And those days﴾, that is, the days of this worldly life: ﴿We alternate them among the people﴾, that is, We turn them among them. We grant victory to these at one time and to those at another time. So it is a present, passing thing, which He distributes among His allies and His enemies. This is unlike the Hereafter, whose gift, victory and hope are purely for those who believe.

Ibn al-Qayyim — may his secret be sanctified — said, in mentioning some of the wise purposes and praiseworthy ends that were in the battle of Uhud:

Among them: the wisdom and custom of Allah regarding His messengers and their followers is that they are made to prevail at one time and are overcome at another, but the final outcome is theirs. For if they were always victorious, the Muslims and others would enter with them, and the truthful would not be distinguished from others. And if they were always defeated, the purpose of the mission and the message would not be achieved. So the wisdom of Allah required that He combine the two matters for them, so that those who follow them and obey them for the truth and what they brought would be distinguished from those who follow them only for dominance and victory. — End.

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And that Allah may know those who believe﴾. Ibn al-Qayyim said: another wisdom, namely that the believers be distinguished from the hypocrites, so that He knows them with the knowledge of seeing and witnessing, after they had been known in His unseen (knowledge). That unseen knowledge (p-981) does not entail reward or punishment; rather, these are entailed upon the known when it becomes witnessed and actual in perception.

A subtle point:

In the verse there are two aspects:

The first: that the thing being explained is omitted, its meaning being: ﴿And that He may know﴾, etc., (we did) that.

The second: that the cause is omitted, and this is coordinated with it, its meaning being: and We did that so that such-and-such would occur, and so that Allah may know. It was omitted to signal that the benefit in what He did is not one, to console them for what befell them, and to make them perceive that a servant is distressed by the calamities that befall him and does not realize that Allah has in that benefits of which he is unaware. — related by al-Zamakhshari.

Caution:

In this verse there is a well-known discussion, namely that its apparent meaning implies that He, the Exalted, did that in order to acquire this knowledge, and it is known that this is impossible for Allah, the Exalted. A similar difficulty is His words, the Exalted: ﴿Or do you think you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known...﴾ [Al Imran: 142], etc. And His words: ﴿And We certainly tested those before them, so that Allah would know those who are truthful and would know the liars﴾ [al-Ankabut: 3]; and His words: ﴿to know which of the two parties is more accurate in computing the time﴾ [al-Kahf: 12]; and His words: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those who strive among you and the patient, and We test your reports﴾ [Muhammad: 31]; (p-982) and His words: ﴿except that We might know who follows the Messenger﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143].

Al-Razi said: Hisham ibn al-Hakam argued from the apparent meanings of these verses that Allah, the Exalted, does not know the occurrence of events except at the time they occur. He said: all these verses indicate that He, the Exalted, only became knowing of these things at the time of their occurrence.

Since the decisive proofs indicate the eternity of His knowledge, may His name be exalted, the scholars answered that with several responses:

Among them: that these are of the category of figurative expression. The meaning in this verse is: that He treats you as one who wishes to know the sincere ones who stand firm in faith from others.

Among them: that "knowledge" here is a metaphor for distinguishing, by way of naming the cause for the effect; that is: that He may distinguish those who remain firm in faith from others.

Among them: that knowledge is in its true sense, but it is considered in terms of its relation to the known, insofar as it is existing and actual: that is, that He may know the firm one as having actually occurred from them, just as He knew that it would occur; for reward falls upon what has occurred, not upon the known that has not yet come into being. This is what Ibn al-Qayyim relied upon, as we quoted at the beginning.

Among them: that the speech is elliptical, with an omitted modifier: that He may know the allies of Allah, and He attributed them to Himself as an honouring. And Allah knows best.

Then He mentioned another wisdom, namely His taking martyrs from among them, by His words: ﴿and that He may take from among you martyrs﴾, that is: and that He may honour some of you with martyrdom, so that they may be an example to others in sacrificing themselves for the sake of the truth, in striving to the utmost for it, and in exalting His word. He, the Exalted, loves the martyrs among His servants, and has prepared for them the highest (p-983) and best of abodes, and has taken them for Himself, so He must grant them the rank of martyrdom. In the term "taking" (ittikhadh), which indicates selection and drawing near, there is an honouring of them and a magnifying of their station that is not hidden. His words: ﴿And Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾ — Ibn al-Qayyim said: a very subtle allusion indicating that His dislike and hatred are for the hypocrites who withdrew from His Prophet on the Day of Uhud and did not witness it, and He did not take martyrs from among them, because He did not love them; so He turned them back and sent them away, to deprive them of what was granted to the believers on that day and what He gave to those among them who were martyred. He thus hindered these wrongdoers from the means which He granted to His allies and His party. End.

So the allusion is to the hypocrites — and it may also be to the disbelievers to whom victory was granted — as a reminder that this was not by way of support for them, but because of the benefits that return to the believers. Then He mentioned another wisdom in what befell them that day, by His words:

The discussion concerning His words, Exalted is He:

[141] ﴿And that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers.﴾

﴿And that Allah may purify those who believe﴾ means: that He may cleanse them and free them from sins and from the afflictions of the souls. Also, He purified and refined them from the hypocrites, so they were distinguished from them. Thus they gained two purifications: a purification from their own souls, and a purification from those who used to show that they were of them while being an enemy. Then He mentioned another wisdom, which is the destruction of the disbelievers, by His words: ﴿and destroy the disbelievers﴾, meaning: He annihilates them. For when they prevail, they transgress and become insolent. That becomes the cause of their ruin and destruction, for it is the custom of Allah, Exalted is He, that when He wills to destroy His enemies and annihilate them, He provides for them the causes by which they deserve their destruction and annihilation. Among the greatest of these causes, after their disbelief, is their transgression and tyranny in harming His allies, fighting them, making war upon them, and empowering themselves over them. Al-mahq (annihilation) is the going away of a thing entirely, such that nothing of it is seen. Allah indeed annihilated those who fought the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the Day of Uhud and persisted in disbelief altogether. Then Allah, Exalted is He, denounced their presumption and their thinking that they would enter Paradise without striving in His cause and enduring the harm of His enemies, and that this is impossible, such that whoever thinks and presumes it is rebuked. He said:

(p-984)

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 142:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[142] ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who strove and known the patient?﴾

﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who strove and known the patient?﴾ That is: "and while that has not yet occurred from you, so that He knows it. For if it had occurred, He would have known it and rewarded you for it with Paradise. Thus the reward is for what has actually occurred and become known, not for mere knowledge, for Allah does not reward the servant merely for His knowledge of it unless what He knows has actually taken place." This was conveyed by Ibn al-Qayyim.

In al-Kashshaf: ﴿wa-lamma yaʿlami Allahu﴾ means: "and while you have not yet struggled," because knowledge is related to the object of knowledge, so the negation of knowledge is placed in the position of the negation of its object, since it is negated along with its negation. A man says: "Allah has known no good in so-and-so," meaning: "there is no good in him, so that He would know it." And (lammā) has the meaning of (lam), except that it carries a kind of expectation, so it indicates the negation of striving in the past and the expectation of it in the future. You say: "He promised me that he would do such-and-such, but not yet (wa-lammā)," meaning: "he has not yet done it, and I expect his doing it."

A subtle point:

Abu Muslim said regarding ﴿Or did you think﴾ that it is a prohibition expressed with the interrogative particle that comes for rebuke. Its summary is: "Do not think that you will enter Paradise while striving has not occurred from you." It is like His words: ﴿Alif. Lam. Mim.﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 1] ﴿Do people think they will be left to say "We have believed" and they will not be tested?﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 2]. He opened the speech with (am), which is most often used in their speech between two options, one of which is in doubt without being specified. They say: "Did you strike Zayd or ʿAmr?" while being certain that the striking happened to one of them. He said: It is the custom of the Arabs to use this kind of interrogation for emphasis. When He said: ﴿And do not weaken nor grieve﴾ [Al ʿImran: 139], it was as if He said: "Do you know that this is as you are commanded, or do you think that you will enter Paradise without striving and patience?" This was deemed unlikely because Allah, exalted is He, had made striving obligatory before this event, made patience obligatory in bearing its hardships, and clarified the aspects of its benefits in religion (p-985) and in this world. Given this, it is far-fetched that a person reaches happiness and Paradise while neglecting this obedience. End of quote.

Then He rebuked them for their defeat, concerning a matter they used to wish for and desire to meet, saying:

The discussion of the Almighty's saying:

[143] ﴿And you certainly used to wish for death before you encountered it; and now you have seen it while you were looking on.﴾

﴿And you certainly used to wish for death﴾: that is, war, for it is among its beginnings; or it means death through martyrdom. ﴿Before you encountered it﴾: that is, you witnessed it and came to know its terror. ﴿Now you have seen it﴾: that is, what you used to wish for of the causes of death; or death through witnessing its customary causes; or the killing of your brothers before your eyes. ﴿While you were looking on﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun of those addressed. The choice of the word "seeing" (ru'yah) over "meeting" (mulaqah), and restricting it to "looking" (naẓar), is an intensification of their witnessing of it.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: When Allah the Exalted informed them through His Prophet of the honour He had bestowed upon the martyrs of Badr, they desired martyrdom, so they wished for a battle in which they would be martyred and join their brothers. Allah showed them that on the Day of Uhud and brought it about for them, but they soon fled, except those whom Allah willed among them. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And you certainly used to wish for death﴾, the verse.

It is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not wish to meet the enemy, but ask Allah for well-being; and when you do meet them, be steadfast, and know that Paradise is under the shade of the swords."

(p-986) The scholars of the military campaigns (ahl al-maghazi) said: When those among the Muslims who fled on the Day of Uhud fled, ʿAbdullah ibn Qamiʾah came forward intending to kill the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr (may Allah be pleased with him), who on that day was the bearer of his banner, defended him, and Ibn Qamiʾah killed him, believing that he had killed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So he returned and said: "I have killed Muhammad." And Satan cried out: "Verily, Muhammad has been killed." This fell into the hearts of many people, and weakness, feebleness and hesitation from fighting occurred. Concerning that, Allah the Exalted revealed:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[144] ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all, and Allah will reward the grateful.﴾

﴿Muhammad is only a messenger﴾. Some of the messengers died and some were killed, so there is no contradiction between being a messenger and being killed or dying, since ﴿messengers have passed away before him﴾, and he will pass away as they did. ﴿So if he dies﴾, meaning: Will you believe in him only during his lifetime? ﴿Or if he is killed, will you turn back﴾, meaning: will you apostatize, ﴿on your heels﴾, meaning: after your knowledge that the messengers before him passed away and that their religion remains, to which one holds fast. ﴿And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all﴾; he only harms himself by exposing himself to wrath and punishment. ﴿And Allah will reward the grateful﴾ with victory and dominance in this world, and with reward and good pleasure in the Hereafter. They are those who did not turn back, but stood in obedience to Him, fought for His religion, and followed His Messenger, alive and dead. He called them grateful because they gave thanks (p-987) for the blessing of Islam, which is the greatest blessing and the most honourable favour. The meaning is that whoever is certain of his religion and insightful regarding his Lord does not apostatize when the Messenger dies or is killed, nor does he slacken in what he was upon, because he strives for his Lord, not for the Messenger, like the companions of the earlier prophets. As Anas (the uncle of Anas ibn Malik) said on the day of Uhud, when the news of the killing of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was spread and reported, the Muslims were routed, and word reached him of some of them saying: "Would that so-and-so could get us safe conduct from Abu Sufyan," and of the hypocrites' saying: "If he had been a prophet, he would not have been killed": "O people, if Muhammad has been killed, the Lord of Muhammad is alive and does not die. What will you do with life after the Messenger of Allah? Fight for what he fought for, and die upon what he died upon." Then he said: "O Allah, I apologize to You for what these say, and I disown what these have brought." Then he drew his sword, fought until he was killed. (Related by al-Qashani.)

(p-988) Ibn Abi Najih narrated from his father that a man from the Emigrants passed by a man from the Helpers who was writhing in his blood, and said to him: "O so-and-so! Did you know that Muhammad ﷺ has been killed?" The Helper said: "If Muhammad has been killed, he has conveyed the message; so fight for your religion." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Muhammad is only...﴾, the verse. Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi related it in (Dala'il al-Nubuwwa).

The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in (Zad al-Ma'ad):

Among them, that is, among the aims in this military campaign, is that the event of Uhud was a prelude and a foretaste before the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So He informed them and reproached them for turning back on their heels if the Messenger of Allah ﷺ should die or be killed. Rather, it is obligatory for them to remain firm upon his religion and his monotheism, to die upon it and to be killed upon it, for they worship the Lord of Muhammad, who is alive and does not die. If Muhammad dies or is killed, it is not fitting that this should divert them from his religion and what he brought. Every soul will taste death, and Muhammad ﷺ was not sent to them to be made immortal, neither he nor they; rather, that they might die upon Islam and monotheism, for death is inevitable. Whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dies or remains is the same. For this reason He reproached those among them who turned back from their religion when Satan shouted that Muhammad had been killed, so He said: ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger﴾, the verse. The grateful are those who recognised the value of the blessing, so they remained steadfast upon it until they died or were killed. Thus the effect of this rebuke and the ruling of this address became manifest on the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, when whoever apostatized turned back on his heels, and the grateful remained steadfast upon their religion. So Allah helped them, honoured them, granted them victory over their enemies, and made the final outcome theirs. (End of quotation.)

It is established in the Sahih that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) recited this verse on the day of the death of the Prophet ﷺ, and all the people recited it from him. The hadith is well known. Then Allah, may He be exalted, informed that He has appointed for every soul a term which it must complete and reach. So all people will come to the watering place of death as one single arrival, though its causes vary, and they will depart from the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection in different directions: a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze, by His saying:

(p-989)

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 145:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[145] ﴿And it is not for a soul to die except by the permission of Allah, at a decreed term. And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof. And We will reward the grateful.﴾

﴿And it is not for a soul to die except by the permission of Allah﴾, i.e., by His command and His will. ﴿At a decreed term﴾ is a verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing the meaning of what precedes it, i.e., He has decreed for every soul its lifespan as a writ fixed to a known time, which neither advances nor delays. In the verse there is an encouragement to the cowardly and an incitement to them to fight, for advancing or holding back does not diminish from one's lifespan nor add to it. ﴿And whoever desires﴾, i.e., by his deed, ﴿the reward of this world, We will give him thereof﴾, i.e., whatever We wish to give him, and he will have no share in the Hereafter; this is an allusion to those who were present seeking the spoils of war. ﴿And whoever desires﴾, i.e., by his deed, ﴿the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof. And We will reward the grateful.﴾ A parallel to this verse is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him thereof, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Shura: 20], and His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Whoever desires the hasty [life], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will enter, blamed and banished﴾ [al-Isra: 18]. ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its proper striving while he is a believer – those, their striving is ever appreciated﴾ [al-Isra: 19].

Know that the verse, although its context concerns jihad, is general in all deeds, because what is effective in bringing reward or punishment is the intentions and motives, not the outward appearances of deeds. Then He rebuked them for their shortcoming and their evil conduct in turning away from the ways of the godly fighters in the cause of Allah alongside the earlier Messengers – peace be upon them – with His saying:

(p-990)

**The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:**

[146] ﴿And how many a prophet fought, and with him fought many devoted people (ribbiyyun). They did not falter for what befell them in the way of Allah, nor did they weaken, nor did they submit. And Allah loves the patient.﴾

﴿And how many a prophet fought, and with him fought many devoted people﴾: that is, how many prophets fought alongside them, to raise the word of Allah and to strengthen His religion, and their companions were the pious worshippers. ﴿They did not falter﴾: that is, they did not weaken, ﴿for what befell them in the way of Allah﴾: of wounds and the martyrdom of some of them, because what befell them was in the way of Allah, in His obedience, in upholding His religion, and in supporting His Messenger. ﴿Nor did they weaken﴾: that is, in jihad, against the enemy, or in the religion. ﴿Nor did they submit﴾ to the enemies, but they were patient in fighting them. ﴿And Allah loves the patient﴾ in fighting His enemies.

**Remarks:**

**First:** *Ka'ayyin* (ka'ayyin, an Arabic word meaning "how many") is in the sense of *kam* (kam, "how many") used for information. It has several dialectal forms. Among the seven canonical readings (al-qira'at al-sab'), Ibn Kathir (Ibn Kathir) read *kā'in* with a long vowel and a hamza, while the rest read it with a doubled consonant (*shadda*). There is much discussion of its meaning, its forms, its widely transmitted and irregular readings, both in continuous recitation (wasl) and in pause (waqf), and of its written form. Consult the entries on these matters.

**Second:** Among the seven readings, *qutila* (qutila, "was killed") is read in the passive voice, with *ribbiyyūn* (ribbiyyūn) as the deputy subject (nā'ib al-fā'il) with certainty. As for the possibility that the pronoun refers to *nabiyy* (nabiyy, "prophet") and that *ma'ahu ribbiyyūn* (ma'ahu ribbiyyūn, "with him are devoted people") is a circumstantial clause (hal), or that it is by way of inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), meaning: "And how many a prophet, with whom are devoted people, was killed", this is a forced reading that sound understanding turns away from, and an arbitrary reading from which the revelation must be exempted. Al-Qaffal (al-Qaffal) transmitted it and al-Suhayli (al-Suhayli) supported it and exaggerated in its favor, but not every black thing is a date (fa-ma kullu sawda'a tamra).

**Third:** *Ribbiyyūn* (ribbiyyūn), with a kasra on the *rā'*, is the reading of the majority. It was also read with a *ḍamma* and with a *fatḥa*. The *fatḥa* is according to the regular pattern, while the kasra and the ḍamma are changes in the relative form (taghyirat al-nisba). They are the *rabbāniyyūn* (rabbāniyyūn, "those devoted to the Lord"), that is, those who worship the Lord, exalted is He.

Then, after explaining their praiseworthy deeds, He, glorified is He, informed of their praiseworthy statements, which are what the prophets and their peoples sought help by against their people: acknowledgment, repentance, seeking forgiveness, and asking their Lord to make their feet firm and to grant them victory over their enemy. He said:

(p-٩٩١)

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[147] ﴿And their words were only that they said: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affair, make firm our feet, and give us victory over the disbelieving people."﴾

﴿And their words were﴾ i.e., these godly men (al-Rabbaniyyun), not like the words of the hypocrites nor of those who were self-conceited. As for "qawlahum" (their words), with the accusative vowel, it is the predicate of "kana" (was), and its subject is "an" (that) together with what follows it in His words, exalted is He: ﴿only that they said: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affair, make firm our feet, and give us victory over the disbelieving people."﴾

Ibn al-Qayyim said: When the people knew that the enemy only gains over them because of their sins, and that Satan only causes them to slip and defeats them through these, and that sins are of two kinds: a shortcoming in a right owed, or a transgression of a limit; and that victory is tied to obedience, they said: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affair﴾. Then they knew that their Lord, blessed and exalted, if He did not make their feet firm and grant them victory, they would not be able to make their own feet firm or give themselves victory over their enemies. So they asked Him for what they knew was in His hand alone, not theirs, and that if He did not make their feet firm and grant them victory, they would not stand firm nor be victorious. Thus they fulfilled both stations their due: the station of what is required, which is tawhid and turning to Him, glorified is He; and the station of removing what prevents victory, which is sins and excess. [End of quotation.]

Al-Qadi said: This is a lesson from God, exalted is He, in the manner of seeking through supplications at times of calamity and trial, whether in jihad or otherwise.

The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[148] ﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter. And Allah loves the good-doers.﴾

﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world﴾: this includes victory, booty, the subjugation of the enemy, good repute, the expansion of the breast through the light of faith, and the expiation of misdeeds. ﴿And the excellent reward of the Hereafter﴾: this is Paradise and the lasting bliss within it. The attribution of excellence to the reward of the Hereafter specifically indicates its virtue and distinction, and that it is what counts with Allah, Exalted is He, unlike this world, because of its scarcity, its mixture with harms, and its being transient and passing away. (p-992) ﴿And Allah loves the good-doers﴾ indicates that what He related of their actions and words is of the category of excellence.

Al-Razi said: In this there is a subtle point. When these people acknowledged their own wrongdoing by saying, ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins﴾ [Al 'Imran: 147], and so on, Allah named them "good-doers," as if Allah, Exalted is He, were saying to them: "When you acknowledge your wrongdoing and your inability, I describe you with excellence and make you a beloved of Myself, so that you know that there is no way for the servant to reach the presence of Allah except by manifesting humility, neediness, and incapacity."

Then, after encouraging them to follow the helpers of the prophets, which leads to the happiness of both abodes, He, glory be to Him, warned them against obeying their enemy. He informed them that if they obeyed them, they would lose both this world and the Hereafter. In this there is an allusion to the hypocrites who obeyed the polytheists when they gained the upper hand and were victorious on the Day of Uhud, by His saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 3, verse 149:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[149] ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels﴾ That is, to polytheism (shirk). Al-irtidad 'ala al-'aqib (turning back on one's heels) is a sign of an affair being reversed, and a proverb for returning after having been in order (al-hawr ba'da al-kawr). ﴿So you will become losers﴾ of the religion of Islam, and of the love of God, His pleasure and His reward, both worldly and otherworldly. So do not believe that they will befriend you as you befriend them. Some of the exegetes said: the fruit of the verse is the indication that the believers must not submit to the ruling of the disbelievers, nor obey them, nor accept their counsel, for fear that they will bring them down from their religion.

(p. 993)

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[150] ﴿Nay, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.﴾

﴿Nay, Allah is your Protector﴾, so obey Him. ﴿And He is the best of helpers﴾, Who will give you victory better than their help would have been had they helped you. And how could He not be the best of helpers, when He gives you victory without fighting, as He promised in His saying:

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[151] ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾, meaning the terror that prevents them from attacking you and from advancing against your sanctuary. ﴿Because they associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority﴾, meaning: by ascribing to Him divinity, or attributes of His, or worthiness of worship. ﴿Authority﴾, meaning: a decisive proof upon which beliefs are based. ﴿Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers.﴾ The *mathwā* (abode) is the dwelling place, the refuge, and the place of residence, from *thawā yathwī* (to dwell).

**Subtleties:**

**The first:** The verse indicates that this terror is due to the associating (shirk) that is in their hearts, and the terror is in proportion to the shirk. Al-Qashani said: The casting of terror into the hearts of the disbelievers is made a consequence of their associating, because courage and the other virtues are balances in the powers of the soul, which are illuminated by the light of tawhid (monotheism). Thus they are not complete except for the monotheist who is certain in his monotheism. As for the associator, he is veiled from the unassailable power because of what he has associated with Allah of existence mixed with non-existence, which in itself has no power, and Allah has sent down no proof for its existence. So he has nothing but weakness, cowardice, and all the vices.

Al-Qaffal, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is as if it were said: Although this incident befell you on the day of Uhud (p-994), Allah, exalted is He, will cast terror from you after that into the hearts of the unbelievers until He subdues the disbelievers and makes your religion prevail over all other religions. Allah has done that, until the religion of Islam became dominant over all religions and creeds. End quote.

It is established in the two Sahihs from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things that no one before me among the prophets was given: I was made victorious through terror over a distance of one month's journey; the earth has been made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification, so whichever man of my nation is overtaken by the time of prayer, let him pray; the spoils of war have been made lawful for me, whereas each prophet used to be sent only to his own people, but I have been sent to all mankind; and I have been given intercession."

**The second:** Mentioning that no proof has been sent down, while it is impossible for such proof to exist in itself, is an indication of its negation and the negation of its being sent down together, because that for which He has sent down no authority has no authority.

**The third:** Abu al-Su'ud said: The verse contains a notification that what is followed in this matter is the heavenly proof, not opinions and false desires.

Al-Razi preceded him to this when he said: This verse indicates the invalidity of blind imitation (taqlid). That is because the verse indicates that shirk has no proof for it, so it must be that the claim of it is false. This is only valid if the claim of affirming what has no proof for its establishment is false, and it follows that blind imitation is invalid. End quote.

Then He informed them that He had fulfilled His promise to them of victory over their enemy, and He is the one who fulfills promises. He told them that if they had persisted in obedience and adhered to the command of the Messenger, their victory would have continued. But they departed from obedience and left their position, so victory left them. Thus He turned them away from their enemy as a punishment and a trial, and to make them know the evil consequences of disobedience and the good consequences of obedience, by His saying:

(p-995)

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[152] ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them that He might test you. And He has already pardoned you, and Allah is full of bounty toward the believers.﴾

﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you﴾ — in His saying: ﴿And if you are patient and fear Allah, their plotting will not harm you at all﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 120]. ﴿When you were killing them﴾ — i.e., you were killing them in great numbers. From (ḥassahu), when one annuls his sense (ḥiss), i.e., destroys it. ﴿By His permission﴾ — i.e., by His facilitation and granting of success. ﴿Until when you lost courage﴾ — i.e., you became weak and slack, inclining toward the spoils. ﴿And disputed about the matter﴾ — i.e., about remaining at the position. The companions of ʿAbdullah said: "The spoils! O people, the spoils! Your companions have gained the upper hand, so what are you waiting for?" ʿAbdullah ibn Jubayr said: "Have you forgotten what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to you?" They said: "By Allah, we will surely go to the people and take a share of the spoils." When they reached them, their faces were turned away, and they fled in defeat. (Narrated by Imam Ahmad.)

And (al-amr) may mean "the affair" or "the matter," or it may mean that which is opposed to (al-nahy), i.e., the prohibition: that is, that about which you were commanded, namely not to leave the position. ﴿And disobeyed﴾ — i.e., the command of the Messenger that you should not leave if you see us gaining the upper hand over them, and if you see them gaining the upper hand over us, then do not help us. (Narrated by al-Bukhari.) ﴿After He had shown you that which you love﴾ — i.e., victory, spoils, and the defeat of the enemy. Al-Bukhari related from al-Bara' who said: "We met the polytheists that day, and the Prophet ﷺ had placed a force of archers and appointed ʿAbdullah ibn Jubayr over them, and said: 'Do not leave if you see us gaining the upper hand over them'," in the wording previously mentioned. Then al-Bara' said: "When we met them, they fled, until I saw the women running up the mountain, lifting their skirts, their anklets exposed, and they began to say: 'The spoils! The spoils!' ..." (the hadith). ﴿Among you are those who desire this world﴾ — i.e., the spoils, so he left the position. ﴿And among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾ — so he remained steadfast in it, and they are those who attained the honor of martyrdom. Among them was Anas ibn al-Nadr, the lion, the bold warrior, who said at that time: "O Allah! I apologize to You for what these people have done" — meaning the Muslims — "and I disavow to You what the polytheists have brought." Then he advanced with his sword, met Saʿd ibn Muʿadh and said: "Where are you, O Saʿd? Indeed I smell the fragrance of Paradise beyond Uhud!" He went forward and was killed, and he was not recognized until his sister recognized him by a mark or by his fingertips, and there were eighty-some wounds on him from stabbing, striking, and arrow shots. This is the wording of al-Bukhari, and Muslim narrated it similarly. May Allah be pleased with him, make him pleased, and sanctify his pure soul. ﴿Then He turned you away from them﴾ — i.e., He restrained you from them until the situation changed and the state turned. There is in this such kindness toward the Muslims as is not hidden. ﴿That He might test you﴾ — i.e., that He might make that turning away a trial for you, so that you would repent to Allah, return to Him, and seek His forgiveness for what you opposed of His command and inclined toward the spoils. Then He informed them that He had pardoned them by His saying: ﴿And He has already pardoned you﴾ — i.e., by way of grace toward you because of your faith. ﴿And Allah is full of bounty toward the believers﴾ — i.e., in all circumstances, whether through victory or through trial, for trial is a bounty and hidden kindness, so that they might train themselves in patience in hardships, steadfastness in the battlefields, and become firm in certainty, making it a settled disposition for them, and realize that Allah does not change what is with a people until they change what is within themselves, and that they should not incline to this world and its adornments, nor be heedless of the truth. It also serves as an immediate punishment for some, so that they are purified of their sins and attain the rank of martyrdom, meeting Allah as victors. (Related by al-Qashani.)

Subtleties:

The first: (idhā) in His saying ﴿until when you lost courage﴾ is either a conditional particle or not. On the first view, its response is either omitted or stated. Its estimate, if omitted: "until when you lost courage, quarreled about the matter, and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love, Allah withheld His victory from you" — because the beginning of the verse indicates it — or "you became two groups," since His saying ﴿Among you are those who desire﴾ etc. conveys its meaning and fulfills its sense. If it is stated, then it is either ﴿and disobeyed﴾ with the "wāw" being extra (ṣila), which is reported from the Kufans and al-Farrā'. They said: its parallel is His saying ﴿So when they both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103] ﴿and We called to him: O Abraham﴾ [al-Saffat: 104], meaning: We called to him.

Some who supported this view claimed that among the practices of the Arabs is the insertion of "wāw" in the response of (ḥattā idhā), based on His saying ﴿until when they reach it and its gates are opened﴾ [al-Zumar: 73], meaning: its gates were opened. They answered the objection that it entails explaining a thing by itself — since failure and quarreling are disobedience, how can they be its cause — by saying that the intended disobedience is their leaving that place. Undoubtedly, failure and quarreling are what caused them to leave it, so there is no circularity. Or it is His saying ﴿then He turned you away from them﴾, with "thumma" being extra — said by Abu Muslim.

On the second view, i.e., that it is not a conditional, then it is a noun, and (ḥattā) is a preposition meaning "until," governing its connection to His saying ﴿He had already fulfilled﴾ (ṣadaqakum) by way of its implicit sense of victory, as if it were said: "Allah had indeed granted you victory until the time of your failure and quarreling."

The second: The benefit of His saying ﴿after He had shown you that which you love﴾ is to draw attention to the magnitude of the disobedience, for when they witnessed that Allah had honored them by fulfilling the promise, it was their duty to refrain from disobedience; when they nevertheless proceeded into it, they were deprived of that honor.

The third: The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿And He has already pardoned you﴾ is that He pardoned them without repentance, since it is not mentioned; this indicates that Allah may pardon the people of major sins.

The fourth: In His saying ﴿and Allah is full of bounty toward the believers﴾ there is evidence that the perpetrator of a major sin is a believer, for the sin in the verse was a major sin — and Allah knows best.

Then Exalted is He reminded them of their state at the time of flight by His saying:

(p-999)

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[153] ﴿When you were climbing up and not turning aside for anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you, so He rewarded you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve over what escaped you nor over what afflicted you. And Allah is Aware of what you do.﴾

"Idh tus'idūna" (when you were climbing) is connected either to "sarafakum" (He turned you away), or to His saying "liyabtaliyakum" (to test you), or to an implied verb. Al-is'ād (ascending) means going far into the land; that is, you were going far in flight. It is also read "tusʿidūna" from the triliteral form, meaning: into the mountain. ﴿Wa lā talwūna﴾ means you did not turn back to stand firm; ﴿ʿalā aḥad﴾ means for anyone, whether near or far, out of bewilderment and terror. ﴿Wa-r-rasūlu yadʿūkum fī ukhrākum﴾ means that he was calling you from your rear and your other group, to abandon fleeing from the enemies and to return and charge against them, while you were retreating, and he was steadfast in his place, in the face of the enemy, with a small group, trusting in Allah's promise and watching over Him.

As-Suddi said: When the polytheists pressed hard upon the Muslims at Uhud and defeated them, some of them entered Madina, and some of them went up the mountain, above the rock, and stood upon it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began calling the people: "To me, servants of Allah! To me, servants of Allah!" So Allah mentioned their climbing up the mountain, then He mentioned the Prophet's (ﷺ) calling them, saying: "When you were climbing," and so on.

Ibn Kathir said: Likewise said Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada, al-Rabiʿ and Ibn Zayd.

In the hadith of al-Bara' (may Allah be pleased with him) in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, when they were routed, there remained with the Prophet (ﷺ) only twelve men. Muslim related from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was left alone on the Day of Uhud with seven from the Ansar and two men from Quraysh.

﴿Fa-athābakum﴾ means He recompensed you for this fleeing and retreat; ﴿ghaman bi-ghamm﴾ means grief continuous upon grief: the grief of defeat and breaking, and the grief of the Satan's shout among them that Muhammad had been killed. It is said: the "bi" means "with"; it is said: it means "upon"; both are close to the first meaning. It is also said: the "bi" is for exchange and recompense, meaning: He made you taste grief in exchange for a grief you caused the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which was your disobedience to his command. This was said by al-Zajjaj. Al-Hasan said: He means the grief of the Day of Uhud for the Muslims in exchange for the grief of the Day of Badr for the polytheists. It is also said: the meaning is grief after grief, that is, multiplied grief.

Then He pointed to the secret of this by His saying: ﴿so that you would not grieve over what escaped you﴾, meaning: so that you would train yourselves in patience under hardships, and steadfastness in them, and accustom yourselves to seeing victory, triumph and booty, and that all things come from Allah and not from yourselves; so do not grieve over what escaped you of fortunes and benefits. And His saying: ﴿nor over what afflicted you﴾ refers to the griefs and harms.

The scholar Ibn al-Qayyim said in Zad al-Ma'ad: It is also said: He recompensed you with grief for what you caused His Messenger of grief by your fleeing from him and your abandoning him to his enemy. So the grief that befell you was a recompense for the grief you inflicted upon His Prophet. The first statement is more apparent, for several reasons:

First: His saying: ﴿so that you would not grieve over what escaped you nor over what afflicted you﴾ is an indication of the wisdom of this grief after grief, which is that it makes them forget grief over what escaped them of victory, and over what afflicted them of defeat and wounds; so by this they forgot the plunder, and this is only achieved through a grief that is followed by another grief.

Second: It corresponds to reality, for they experienced the grief of losing the booty, then followed by the grief of defeat, then the grief of the wounds that afflicted them, then the grief of killing, then the grief of hearing that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been killed, then the grief of their enemies' rising above them on the mountain. The intended meaning is not two griefs specifically, but a continuous grief to complete the trial and testing.

Third: His saying "with grief" (bi-ghamm) is part of the reward, not the cause of the reward. The meaning is: He recompensed you with grief continuous upon grief, as a reward for what occurred from you of fleeing, and abandoning His Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, and not responding to him while he was calling you, and disobeying him by remaining at your post, and disputing over the matter, and your cowardice. Each of these matters necessitates a grief specific to it, so griefs succeeded one another upon them, just as their causes and requirements succeeded one another from them. Had He not overtaken them with His pardon, it would have been something else. And of His gentleness toward them, His compassion and His mercy, is that these matters which proceeded from them were among the matters of natural disposition, being remnants of the souls that prevent steadfast victory; so by His gentleness He arranged for them causes that brought these out from potentiality into actuality, and their disliked consequences followed from them. Then they knew that repentance from them, guarding against their like, and repelling them by their opposites, was a necessity without which success and lasting, steadfast victory would not be complete for them. So they became more cautious afterwards and more aware of the doors through which they had been entered. Often bodies are healed by ailments.

A subtle point:

The word "thawāb" (reward) is generally used only for good, though it may also be used for evil, since it is derived from the saying: thāba ilayhi ʿaqluhu (his reason returned to him), meaning it returned to him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when We made the House a place of return for the people﴾ [al-Baqara: 125]. A woman is called thayyib because the one who has intercourse with her returns to her. The origin of thawāb is whatever returns to the doer as the recompense of his action, whether good or bad, but by custom the word thawāb became restricted to good. If we take the word thawāb here according to its linguistic origin, the sentence is sound; if we take it according to customary usage, it comes as a form of mockery, as one says: "His greeting is a blow and his reproach is the sword," meaning he placed grief in the place of what they hoped for of reward, on the pattern of: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 24]. This was said by al-Razi.

A note:

al-Mufaddal said: "lā" is superfluous, and the meaning is: so that you would be grieved over what escaped you and over what afflicted you as a punishment for you, like His saying: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾ [al-A'raf: 12] and ﴿so that the People of the Scripture may know﴾ [al-Hadid: 29], meaning: that you should prostrate and that they may know.

In my view this is far-fetched, especially with the repetition of "lā" in the conjoined phrase, and the sound meaning being consistent when it is considered a negation; so the correct view is what has preceded.

﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, good and bad, Able to recompense you. In it is the greatest deterrent against undertaking disobedience. Then He, glorified is He, overtook them with His mercy, and lightened that grief for them, and made it pass from them by the drowsiness He sent down upon them as security from Him, as He said:

The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[154] ﴿Then after the distress He sent down security upon you, drowsiness overcoming a group of you, while another group was concerned only for themselves, thinking about God other than the truth, the thoughts of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance). They say, "Do we have any say in the matter?" Say, "Indeed, the matter belongs entirely to God." They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you. They say, "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here." Say, "Even if you had been in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their places of death," so that God may test what is in your breasts and purge what is in your hearts. God is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾

﴿Then after the distress He sent down upon you security﴾: that is, safety. "Amanah" (with a vowel on the mim) is a verbal noun. It is said: amina amnan, amanan, amanan, and amanah (with both vowels). In the hadith about the descent of ʿIsa (peace be upon him), "amanah" occurs in the earth, meaning security. Similar verbal nouns are "al-ʿazamah" and "al-ghalabah", and it is in the accusative as an object. His words, ﴿drowsiness﴾, are a substitute for "amanah." It is also said that it is the object, and "amanah" is a circumstantial accusative or an object of purpose. ﴿Overcoming a group of you﴾: they are the sincere ones, the people of certainty, steadfastness and true reliance on God, who are firmly convinced that God, Mighty and Majestic, will support His Messenger and fulfil his hope. Drowsiness during war is a sign of safety, as He said in the surah of al-Anfal: ﴿When He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him﴾ [al-Anfal: 11], and so on.

Al-Bukhari related in the Tafsir, from Anas, from Abu Talhah, who said: "Drowsiness overtook us while we were in our battle lines on the day of Uhud. He said: My sword kept falling from my hand, and I would pick it up, and it would fall, and I would pick it up again." It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim. The wording of al-Tirmidhi is: Abu Talhah said: "I lifted my head on the day of Uhud and began to look, and there was not one of them that day who was not swaying beneath his shield from drowsiness. That is His saying: ﴿Then after the distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness.﴾"

Al-Razi has mentioned several benefits of that drowsiness:
Among them: the enemies were intent in the extreme on killing them, so that their remaining asleep, with safety, in such a battle is among the clearest proofs that God's protection and preservation were with them. This removes fear from their hearts and gives them greater trust in God's promise, Exalted is He. End of quotation.

Then God, Exalted is He, informed that whoever was not overcome by that drowsiness was among those whom their own selves had concerned, not their religion, their Prophet or his Companions, by His words: ﴿while another group was concerned only for themselves﴾, that is: their only concern was for themselves, and they were aiming at their own deliverance (p-1005). So drowsiness did not overcome them because of anxiety, distress and fear: ﴿thinking about God other than the truth﴾, that is, other than the true thought that ought to be held about Him, glory be to Him: ﴿the thoughts of the Jahiliyyah﴾, as He said in another verse: ﴿Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families﴾ [al-Fath: 12], and so on. Likewise, these people believed that when the polytheists prevailed at that hour, it was the decisive end, and that Islam and its people had perished. This is the way of people of doubt and suspicion: when a dreadful matter occurs, these vile thoughts arise in them.

The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in Zad al-Ma'ad: This suspicion which is not fitting for God has been explained as meaning that He, glory be to Him, would not support His Messenger, that His cause would be extinguished, and that He would hand him over to death. It has also been explained as meaning that what befell them was not by His decree and destiny, and that He had no wisdom in it. Thus it was explained as denying wisdom, denying divine decree, and denying that He would complete the affair of His Messenger and make it prevail over all religion. This is the evil suspicion which the hypocrites and polytheists held about Him, glory be to Him and exalted, in the surah of al-Fath, where He says: ﴿and that He may punish the hypocrite men and women and the polytheist men and women who think evil thoughts about God. Upon them is the evil circle; God is angry with them, has cursed them, and has prepared for them Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾ [al-Fath: 6]. This was only evil suspicion and the suspicion of the Jahiliyyah attributed to the people of ignorance, and thinking other than the truth, because it is a thought that does not befit His beautiful names, His exalted attributes, and His Essence, which is free of every imperfection. In contrast with what befits His wisdom, His praiseworthiness, His unique lordship and divinity, what befits His true promise which He does not break, and His word which preceded His messengers that He will support them and not forsake them, and that His army are the victorious. Whoever thinks of Him that He does not support His messengers, does not complete His affair, does not strengthen Himself and His army, does not exalt them and grant them victory over their enemies, does not make them prevail over them, and that He does not support His religion and His Book, and that He lets polytheism prevail over monotheism and falsehood over truth (p-1006), with a lasting domination in which monotheism and truth are extinguished, never to rise again, has indeed thought evil of God and attributed to Him what is contrary to His perfection, majesty, attributes and qualities. His might and the wisdom of His divinity reject that, and refuse that He should humiliate His party and His army, or that lasting victory and enduring triumph should belong to His enemies, the polytheists who associate others with Him and who set up equals to Him. Whoever thinks of Him this has not known Him, nor known His names, nor known His attributes and perfection. Likewise, whoever denies that this is by His decree and destiny has not known Him, nor known His lordship, His dominion and His greatness. Likewise, whoever denies that He decreed that and other than that for a far-reaching wisdom and a praiseworthy end, for which He deserves praise, and that this came only from a bare will devoid of wisdom and of a desired end that He loves more than missing it, and that these disliked causes which lead to it do not have their decree outside of wisdom, because they lead to what He loves, even if they are disliked by Him, then He did not decree them in vain, nor create them without purpose, nor create them for nothing: ﴿That is the thought of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ [Sad: 27]. Most people think of God other than the truth, an evil thought, regarding what concerns them and what He does to others. No one is safe from that except one who knows God, knows His names and attributes, and knows what His praise and wisdom require. Whoever despairs of His mercy and gives up on His spirit has thought evil of Him. Whoever holds it permissible for Him to punish His friends despite their goodness and sincerity, and to equate them with His enemies, has thought evil of Him. Whoever thinks that He will leave His creation aimless, without commands and prohibitions, not sending them messengers nor sending down books to them, but leaving them neglected like cattle, has thought evil of Him. Whoever thinks that He will not gather His servants after their death for reward and punishment in an abode where He recompenses the good doer for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil, and makes clear to His creation the reality of what they differed about, and shows to all the worlds His truthfulness and the truthfulness of His messengers, and that His enemies were the liars, has thought evil of Him. Whoever thinks that He will waste the good deed he did, sincerely for His noble face, in obedience to His command, and nullify it without any cause from the servant, and that He punishes him for what he had no part in, no choice, no power and no will in its occurrence, but punishes him for His own act through him, or thinks (p-1007) that it is permissible for Him to support His enemies, who lie about Him, with the miracles with which He supports His prophets and messengers and makes them occur at their hands, so that they mislead His servants by them, and that everything is good from Him, even punishing one who spent his life in obeying Him, making him eternal in the Hellfire at the lowest of the low, and bestowing blessing on one who used up his life in enmity to Him, His messengers and His religion, raising him to the highest of the high, and that both matters are equally good to Him, and that the impossibility of one and the occurrence of the other is known only through a true report, since reason does not decide the ugliness of one and the beauty of the other, has thought evil of Him. Whoever thinks of Him that He has told about Himself, His attributes and His acts with what outwardly is falsehood, likeness and comparison, and has abandoned the truth without telling it, but has only alluded to it with distant symbols and indicated it with puzzling signs, without stating it clearly, and has always stated likeness, comparison and falsehood clearly, and wanted His creatures to tire their minds, powers and thoughts in distorting His speech from its places and interpreting it other than its meaning, seeking for it the far-fetched possibilities and interpretations which resemble riddles and enigmas more than disclosure and clarification, and has referred them, for knowing His names and attributes, to their minds and opinions and not to His Book, and wanted them not to take His speech according to what they know of their own discourse and language, although He is able to state clearly to them the truth that ought to be stated, and relieve them of the words which cause them to believe falsehood, yet He did not do so, but led them away from the path of guidance and clarity, has thought evil of Him. For if he says that He is unable to express the truth in clear words such as those used by himself and his predecessors, he has thought of His power as deficient. And if he says that He is able but did not clarify, and turned away from clarity and from stating the truth plainly, to what gives illusion, indeed to what brings about falsehood which is impossible and corrupt belief, he has thought evil of His wisdom and His mercy. And he has thought that he and his predecessors expressed the truth in its clear form apart from God and His Messenger, and that guidance and truth are in their speech and expressions. As for the speech of God, it is only taken in its outward form as likeness, comparison and misguidance, while the outward form of the speech of the confused and bewildered is guidance and truth. This is among the worst of thoughts about God. All of these are among those who think evil of God, and among those who think of Him other than the truth, the thoughts of the Jahiliyyah. Whoever thinks of Him that there is in His dominion what He does not will and cannot bring into existence and form, has thought evil of Him. Whoever thinks of Him that He was inactive from eternity to eternity, unable to act, and not described at that time as being able to act, and then became able to act after He had not been able, has thought evil of Him. Whoever thinks of Him that He is not above His heavens upon His Throne, separate from His creation, and that the relation of His Essence, exalted is He, to His Throne is like its relation to the lowest of the low and to places that are shunned in mention, and that He is low just as He is high, and whoever says "Glory be to my Lord the Lowest" is like one who says "Glory be to my Lord the Highest," has thought of Him the most hideous thought.

Then he said: In sum, whoever thinks of Him something other than what He described Himself with, and what His messengers described Him with, or nullifies the realities of what He described Himself with and what His messengers described Him with, has thought evil of Him. Whoever thinks that anyone intercedes with Him without His permission, or that between Him and His creation there are intermediaries who raise their needs to Him, or that He has set up for His servants friends besides Him whom they draw near to Him by, and seek means through them to Him, and make them intermediaries between themselves and Him, so that they call upon them, fear them and hope in them, has thought of Him the most hideous and worst thought.

Then he said: Whoever thinks of Him that if one is sincere to Him in desire and fear, humbles himself before Him, asks Him, seeks help from Him and relies upon Him, He will disappoint him and not give him what he asked, has thought evil of Him, and thought of Him other than what He is worthy of.

Then he said: As for one who thinks of Him that if one disobeys Him or angers Him and persists in His disobediences, then takes besides Him a protector, and calls upon besides Him an angel or a human, living or dead, hoping thereby that it will benefit him with his Lord and deliver him from His punishment, then he has thought an evil thought of Him, and that increases him in distance from God and in His punishment. And one who thinks of Him that He empowers His enemies over His Messenger, Muhammad, with a settled and perpetual domination in his life and in his death, and tests him with them, never parting from him; so that when he died they took over the affair to the exclusion of his testament, wronged the People of his House, deprived them of their right, and humiliated them; and the might, the victory and the subjugation remained for his enemies and their enemies perpetually, without any crime or sin on the part of his allies and the People of Truth; while He sees their subjugation of them, their usurpation of their right, and their altering of the religion of their Prophet, and He is able to help His allies, His party and His soldiers, yet does not help them nor grant them the upper hand, but rather grants the upper hand to their enemies over them forever; or [one thinks] that He is not able to do that, and that this happened without His power or His will. Then He made His enemies, who altered His religion, reclining companions in His presence, with His community greeting him and them at every time (as the Rafidah imagine). Then he has thought the most ugly and the worst of thoughts of Him. Whether they say that He is able to help them and grant them dominion and victory, or that He is not able to do so, they are in either case impugning His power or His wisdom and His praiseworthiness, and that is among the evil thoughts of Him. There is no doubt that the Lord who did this is hateful to those who think this of Him, and not praiseworthy in their eyes, and it was obligatory that He should do otherwise. But they patched this corrupt thought with a greater tear, and sought refuge from the scorching sand in the fire, saying: this did not happen by the will of God, and He has no power to repel it or to help His allies, for He is not able to act on the deeds of His servants, and they do not fall under His power. Thus they thought of their Lord the thought of their brothers, the Magians and the Dualists. Every falsifier, disbeliever, innovator, and subjugated oppressed person thinks this thought of his Lord, and that he is more deserving of victory, triumph and exaltation than his opponents. Most of creation, indeed all of them, except whom God wills, think of God other than the truth and an evil thought. For the majority of the children of Adam believe that they are deprived of their right and short of their portion, and that they deserve more than what God has given them; the tongue of their state says: my Lord has wronged me and withheld from me what I deserve, and their soul bears witness to this, while with their tongue they deny it and do not dare to declare it. Whoever examines his soul and delves into knowledge of its hidden depths and inner secrets will see this latent in it, like fire hidden in the flint. Strike the flint of whomever you wish, and its spark will tell you what is in its flint. And if you probed whomever you probe, you would find in him a grievance against destiny, a blame of it, and a demand against it contrary to what has occurred, and that it ought to have been thus and thus; so some consider themselves sufficient and some consider their share great. Examine yourself: are you free of this?

﻿﻿ ﻿
If you are saved from it, you are saved from a great thing; otherwise I do not think you are saved.

So let the discerning, sincere advisor take care of his own soul in this matter, and let him repent to God and seek His forgiveness at all times for his thinking evil of his Lord. Let him think evil of his own self, which is the source of all evil and the spring of all wickedness, built upon ignorance and wrongdoing; it is more deserving of evil thoughts than the Wisest of the wise, the Most Just of the just, the Most Merciful of the merciful, the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs complete self-sufficiency, complete praise, and complete wisdom, exalted above every evil in His essence, attributes, actions and names. His essence has absolute perfection from every aspect, His attributes are likewise, and His actions are likewise; all of them are wisdom, benefit, mercy and justice. His names are all most beautiful. The purpose of what has led us to this discussion is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a group, whom their own souls had concerned, were thinking of God other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah﴾.

Then He informed about the statement that issued from their false thought, with His saying: ﴿They say: Is there anything of the affair for us?﴾ That is: Is there for us any part in the affair of planning and opinion? It is an interrogative in the manner of denial, meaning: we have no command that is obeyed. A parallel to this is what God related of them, that they said: ﴿If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed﴾ [Al 'Imran: 168]. That is because 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, when the Prophet ﷺ consulted him in this event, advised him not to leave Medina; then the Companions insisted upon the Prophet ﷺ that he go out to them, as has passed. When 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy returned with those who were with him, and was informed of the great number of the slain from the Banu al-Khazraj, he said: Is there anything of the affair for us?
